# CREED: everything in one file

> CREED is the Wayne State app stack's written standard: 61 numbered practices, policy.json with the support dates for PHP, Laravel, Node, MySQL, Vue and Inertia, and a small PHP reader that tells a tool what state a version is in on a given day.

The README and the Markdown twin of every page, joined. The index is https://creed.apps.wayne.edu/llms.txt. Written by Squire's agent-ready kit; do not edit.

---

## README

Source: https://github.com/waynestate/creed/blob/HEAD/README.md

## CREED

**The standard everything rests on.** The Wayne State App Stack Code: one policy file, one reader, and an
inspector who stamps what he finds.

**Not to be confused with:** CREED is the rules; PROCTOR checks an app against them.

Checks: `composer ci` (the same command runs on GitLab and GitHub).

Front page: [`site/index.html`](https://github.com/waynestate/creed/blob/HEAD/site/index.html), a static page you can open in a browser or serve from `site/`.
On Citadel it is served by the raw-PHP deploy layer in [`deploy/`](https://github.com/waynestate/creed/blob/HEAD/deploy/): a Squire kit whose front controller serves `site/` behind HELMET's security headers. For local development, keep serving `site/` directly.

One command, two clouds, zero excuses. Higher.

CREED is the Wayne State app stack's version policy, as data. One file,
`policy/policy.json`, lists the support dates for PHP, Laravel, Node, MySQL,
Vue and Inertia, plus the rules every check runs against. A small
framework-free PHP reader, `Waynestate\Creed\Policy`, answers the one question
every tool needs: what state is this version in, on this date?

### Documentation

The documentation site lives at [`site/docs/index.html`](https://github.com/waynestate/creed/blob/HEAD/site/docs/index.html) and deploys to [https://creed.apps.wayne.edu/docs/](https://creed.apps.wayne.edu/docs/). It is built from `docs/` by Squire's shared docs builder, and `composer ci` fails when the committed pages go stale. Creed Bratton keeps his records in a filing cabinet nobody can find; ours are in `docs/`, where anyone can.

The docs pages are bound into the same code book as the front page: the running head and main menu, the cream stock and green cloth spine, Source Serif and IBM Plex Mono, stamped callouts and the green colophon. Dark mode is the same book read after hours (warm graphite, cream type, gold foil), never a green wallpaper. The cover's gold ribbon marks the page you are reading, and each callout's stamp is pressed as it scrolls in, for readers who allow motion. That look lives in two files, `docs/_header.html` and `docs/theme/creed.css`, named by the `theme` key in `docs/docs.json`; edit those, never the kit's `site/assets/docs.css`.

### Where the code lives

The canonical repository is [enterprise-apps/creed](https://git.wayne.edu/enterprise-apps/creed) on git.wayne.edu: clone it over SSH as `git@git.wayne.edu:enterprise-apps/creed.git`, or over HTTPS as `https://git.wayne.edu/enterprise-apps/creed.git`. Open issues and merge requests there; tags are made there, by the maintainer, with an approver. CI runs on git.wayne.edu.

GitHub ([waynestate/creed](https://github.com/waynestate/creed)) is a read-only push mirror of it: nobody pushes to it, and Packagist reads from it.

Creed Bratton would say the code lives wherever he last left it. Ours lives on git.wayne.edu.

No other code in the stack decides a version's state. The rules live in one
place, and every tool reads them from here.

### Install

```
composer require waynestate/creed
```

#### Develop on it

The same commands work in PowerShell and sh:

- Windows (PowerShell): `composer install`, then `composer ci` for everything CI runs, or `composer test` for just the tests.
- Linux and macOS (sh): the very same three commands, `composer install`, `composer ci`, `composer test`.

With only Docker (the same line works in PowerShell and sh):

```
docker run --rm -v "${PWD}:/app" -w /app composer:2.10.3 sh -c "composer install --no-interaction && composer ci"
docker run --rm -v "${PWD}:/app" -w /app php:8.5-cli vendor/bin/phpunit
```

The whole band fits in three commands, and nobody needs a solo.

### Usage

```php
use Waynestate\Creed\Policy;
use Waynestate\Creed\State;

$policy = Policy::bundled();

// What state is PHP 8.2 in, on this date?
$state = $policy->stateOf('php', '8.2', new DateTimeImmutable('2026-10-27'));
// State::Security

// What is the oldest PHP an app may declare?
$floor = $policy->oldestSupported('php', new DateTimeImmutable('2026-10-27'));
// '8.2'
```

#### Reading the policy from PHP

The reader's public members, one line each:

- `Policy::bundled()`, `Policy::fromFile($path)`, `Policy::fromArray($data)`: load a policy; `origin()` says where it came from.
- `stateOf($component, $version, $on)`: the state, or an exception; `tryStateOf()` is the same answer as `null` when it cannot be answered.
- `oldestSupported($component, $on)`: the lowest version still Active or Security; `supported()` lists all of them, oldest first.
- `latestPatch($component, $version)`: the current patch in that line; `latestPatchChecked()` says when it was last checked.
- `line($component, $version)`: the raw line, with `active_until`, `security_until`, `latest_patch`, `latest_patch_checked` (each a string or null) and `current` (true or null).
- `activeUntil()`, `securityUntil()`: those dates as `DateTimeImmutable`, or null.
- `daysToEol($component, $version, $on)`: whole days until `security_until`, signed; `isPastGrace()` says whether the grace period is over.
- `resolveVersion($component, $version)`: the policy line a full version like `8.3.12` belongs to.
- `isAheadOfPolicy($component, $version)`: whether a version sorts above every line the policy lists.
- `belowOldestLineReason($component, $version)`: the reason a version is `Eol` for sorting below every listed line, or null.
- `hasComponent()`, `components()`, `versions($component)`, `tools()`, `toolMinimum($tool)`, `rules()`: the shape of the policy itself.

One last time: the reader answers, it does not guess.

#### With Arms Wide Open

The support window stays open until `security_until`. A version is still
`Security` on that day, moves to `Eol` the day after, and stays in `Eol` for
`eol_grace_days` (90) more days before it is `EolGraceExpired`. The boundary
is inclusive, and the reader never guesses.

#### Versions CREED hasn't heard of

The reader refuses what it does not know, except the newest thing and the
oldest. A version that sorts above every line the policy lists is `Active`,
and `isAheadOfPolicy()` says so. A version that parses and sorts below every
listed line is `Eol`: it is older than the oldest listed line, and that is
end of life by definition. `belowOldestLineReason()` gives the reason,
`older than the oldest listed line (8.1)`. A version that falls between
listed lines, or that does not parse, is still unknown, and still throws.
Current versions are never refused.

A line marked `"current": true` is `Active` on every date and carries no
`security_until`: the policy says the line is current, and the reader does not
guess when it stops being so.

#### Higher

CREED itself requires PHP `^8.3`, like every stack package, and CI tests it on
8.3, 8.4 and 8.5. The policy's floor for apps is a different number: `^8.2`
until PHP 8.2 reaches end of life on 2026-12-31, then `^8.3`. Creed has always
been one version ahead of everyone else, at least by his own account.

### Proof

Proof runs against real Wayne State applications are on a private
site, [proof.apps.wayne.edu/creed](https://proof.apps.wayne.edu/creed/), behind a Wayne State employee sign-in.

### The handbook

The rules, chapter by chapter, live in [`handbook/`](https://github.com/waynestate/creed/blob/HEAD/handbook/README.md).

### Keeping the patches fresh

`bin/refresh-patches.php` re-reads the upstream feeds, rewrites the
`latest_patch` fields in `policy/policy.json`, and proposes new Vue lines from
endoflife.date. A scheduled CI job runs the refresh and is check-only: when
the policy changed, the tool exits 3 and the job fails on the diff.

The policy robot (`bin/policy-bot.php run`) is the committing path, and it
runs every Monday. It runs the fuller `bin/refresh-policy.php` (below), commits
`policy/policy.json` and `policy/sources.json` on `auto/policy-refresh`, and
force-pushes a merge request titled "policy: refresh from upstream sources",
labeled `auto-data`. After a refresher exit 3 the merge request merges itself
once its pipeline passes; after an exit 4 (something held or refused) it waits
for a person. Each held or refused item, each disagreement between sources the
policy cannot settle, and each listed line within 60 days of its
`security_until` also gets one GitLab issue labeled `auto-alert`, noted on
later runs and closed when it clears. When `refreshed_on` is a week old and
nothing moved, the robot stamps it anyway (the heartbeat). It never tags or
releases, and a missing CI variable stops it before any push. To review a
robot merge request, read its body (one line per change, with its class),
check any date against its source, and never commit to `auto/policy-refresh`:
the next run overwrites it. If its pipeline goes red for an unrelated reason,
fix `main` and rebase the merge request. The [policy robot
guide](https://creed.apps.wayne.edu/docs/guides/policy-bot.html) has the
details.

The `policy-bot` job in `.gitlab-ci.yml` runs the robot on the schedule that
carries `CREED_JOB=policy-bot` and by hand from the web. Without the token the
job prints "CREED_BOT_TOKEN not set; skipping the policy robot" and stays
green. The setup, all on the CREED project on git.wayne.edu (the canonical
repository):

1. A project access token (Settings > Access tokens): role Maintainer
   (Developer works only if Developers may merge to the default branch),
   scopes `api` and `write_repository`, an expiry of 90 days, then rotate.
2. A CI/CD variable `CREED_BOT_TOKEN` holding the token: masked and hidden,
   protected, not a file. The schedule runs on `main`, which is a protected
   branch, so the protected variable is available there.
3. A pipeline schedule on `main` (Build > Pipeline schedules): weekly, Monday,
   with the variable `CREED_JOB` = `policy-bot`.

The branch `auto/policy-refresh` must not be protected, or the robot cannot
push it. The schedules are GitLab project settings, not files in this repo.
The GitHub mirror runs the same check on a cron and on demand.

### Refreshing the policy

`bin/refresh-policy.php` keeps every support date, patch and new line in
`policy/policy.json` tied to a canonical source, so nobody types a date by
hand. PHP dates come from php.net, Node dates from the Node.js release
schedule, and Laravel, MySQL, Vue and Composer from endoflife.date; patches
come from php.net, nodejs.org, Packagist and npm. Each run sorts every change:

| Class | What it is | What happens |
|---|---|---|
| `tighten` | a date moves earlier, or a `current` line gets its first end date | written |
| `neutral` | a new `latest_patch`, or a new line above every listed line | written |
| `loosen-warning` | `active_until` moves later (a warning tier, never a failure) | written |
| `loosen-fail` | `security_until` moves later, or an EOL line would be supported again | held, unless two independent sources agree (php.net and endoflife.date for PHP, schedule.json and endoflife.date for Node) or `policy/sources.json` shows the same value from the same source for 14 days |
| `refused` | removing a line or a date, or any change to `tools` or `rules` | never automatic; reported (a Composer minimum on an EOL line shows up here) |

A source that is down, slow or returns something unreadable changes nothing:
its fields keep their last good value. A line missing from a feed is never
removed. Where a first-party source and endoflife.date disagree, the first
party wins and the disagreement is reported.

```
php bin/refresh-policy.php [--dry-run] [--offline <dir>] [--policy <path>]
    [--sources <path>] [--report <file>] [--today YYYY-MM-DD] [--touch]
```

`--report` writes JSON with `changes`, `held`, `refused`,
`disagreements` and `source_errors`. `--touch` sets `refreshed_on` to today even
when nothing else changed (the weekly heartbeat). `policy/sources.json` records,
per value, which source said it, and the first and last day it was seen.

Exit codes: `0` nothing worth committing (always `0` with `--dry-run`); `1` hard
failure; `3` something was written to `policy/policy.json` or `policy/sources.json`,
including a released `loosen-fail` (the policy robot raises the alert from the
report); `4` something was held or refused (whatever could be written was
written; the held or refused items stay out). The refresher never commits: the
policy robot does.
`bin/refresh-patches.php` still works as before.

### Carrying CREED in another package

PROCTOR, Booster and Rollcall each carry a generated copy of the reader
under their own namespace, so two tools in one app never fight over a class
name (the generator below keeps the copies in step). ADVISOR carries CREED's
policy and handbook as a data bundle instead. The copies began
because CREED was not on Packagist. It is now (`waynestate/creed`, 0.1.7 at this writing), so
each copy can become a real `require`, one consumer at a time; until a
consumer switches, its copy stays. CREED owns the generator and the check:

```
php bin/export.php --namespace=Waynestate\Proctor\Creed --to=vendor/creed-copy
php bin/export.php --check --namespace=Waynestate\Proctor\Creed --to=vendor/creed-copy
```

The copy is the reader with the namespace rewritten and `bundled()` repointed
at its own `policy.json`; `--check` fails when the copy drifts from the source.
Creed Bratton would have a form for this.

### Tests

Maintainers: how to build, test and release this project, and where its data comes from, is in [MAINTAINING.md](https://github.com/waynestate/creed/blob/HEAD/MAINTAINING.md).

No PHP on the machine? Fine. Docker runs the suite:

```
docker run --rm -v "${PWD}:/app" -w /app composer:2.10.3 composer install --no-interaction
docker run --rm -v "${PWD}:/app" -w /app php:8.4-cli vendor/bin/phpunit
docker run --rm -v "${PWD}:/app" -w /app php:8.3-cli vendor/bin/phpunit
```

The policy validates against its schema:

```
docker run --rm -v "${PWD}:/app" -w /app composer:2.10.3 composer validate-policy
```

The site carries an accessibility gate (axe-core in Playwright, WCAG 2.2 AA, run in Docker): `scripts/a11y.sh` on Linux and macOS, `scripts/a11y.ps1` on Windows.

### Strongly recommended: a git.wayne.edu instance runner

git.wayne.edu now has an instance runner, and the stack's CI runs on it.
Every product in the stack still strongly recommends a git.wayne.edu
instance runner, so that capacity stays there.

Creed Bratton, whose quality assurance work we all admire. His past is a
mystery. Ours is in `policy/policy.json`, where it belongs.

---

Wayne State App Stack 2026 Edition Adopted 2026-10-29

## CREED The Wayne State App Stack Code

§0.1 Short title

This code shall be known as CREED, which stands for

C&IT Rules for Every Enterprise Developer

and may be cited as *the standard everything rests on*.

These are the stack's written standards. The handbook has the practices, and `policy.json` has the support dates for PHP, Laravel, Node, MySQL, Vue and Inertia. A small PHP reader takes a version and a day and tells you its state, so PROCTOR, Rollcall and the rest don't each keep their own list of dates.

**Already included in [WELD](https://weld.apps.wayne.edu/).** Install CREED by itself when an app or tool that isn't WELD needs the stack's rules or the dates in `policy.json`.

[Inspect a version](https://creed.apps.wayne.edu/#inspection) [Read the handbook](https://creed.apps.wayne.edu/handbook/)

- **Enforced**: 7
- **Checked**: 14
- **Partially**: 9
- **Documented**: 22
- **Not yet**: 9

Table of contents

### Eleven chapters, 61 practices

Each practice has a reason, its sources and a stamp for how the stack holds it today. Clause numbers follow the chapters, so §2.1 is practice 11 in [BEST_PRACTICES.md](https://github.com/waynestate/creed/blob/main/BEST_PRACTICES.md). This page prints the clauses people ask about most. All 61 are in that file, and the rules themselves are in [the handbook](https://creed.apps.wayne.edu/handbook/).

1. [1 The version policy as data §1.1 to §1.10](https://creed.apps.wayne.edu/#ch-1)
2. [2 PHP and framework versions §2.1 to §2.7](https://creed.apps.wayne.edu/#ch-2)
3. [3 Dependencies §3.1 to §3.6](https://creed.apps.wayne.edu/#ch-3)
4. [4 Secrets and configuration §4.1 to §4.3](https://creed.apps.wayne.edu/#ch-4)
5. [5 Overrides and rollout §5.1 to §5.3](https://creed.apps.wayne.edu/#ch-5)
6. [6 Writing the handbook §6.1 to §6.7](https://creed.apps.wayne.edu/#ch-6)
7. [7 Patching and the supply chain §7.1 to §7.9](https://creed.apps.wayne.edu/#ch-7)
8. [8 Platform and database §8.1 to §8.3](https://github.com/waynestate/creed/blob/main/BEST_PRACTICES.md#8-platform-and-database-second-pass)
9. [9 Policy data §9.1 to §9.3](https://github.com/waynestate/creed/blob/main/BEST_PRACTICES.md#9-policy-data-second-pass)
10. [10 Accessibility and the legal floor §10.1 to §10.3](https://github.com/waynestate/creed/blob/main/BEST_PRACTICES.md#10-accessibility-and-the-legal-floor-second-pass)
11. [11 WSU developer standards §11.1 to §11.7](https://github.com/waynestate/creed/blob/main/BEST_PRACTICES.md#11-wsu-developer-standards-2024)

#### Key to the stamps

- **Enforced**: Code makes the violation impossible, or a test fails CI.
- **Checked**: PROCTOR or CI warns or fails. The check is named.
- **Partially**: Some of it is built or checked. The rest is written down only.
- **Documented**: Written down only.
- **Not yet**: A gap. We print it anyway so you know it's there.

Art. I

#### The policy

`policy/policy.json` holds every support date as an ISO day, plus the rules: an audit threshold of `high`, banned constraints `dev-*` and `*`, and a grace of 90 days. A schema guards it.

Art. II

#### The reader

`Waynestate\Creed\Policy` is plain PHP with no framework. `stateOf` returns `Active`, `Security`, `Eol` or `EolGraceExpired`. No other code in the stack decides a version's state.

Art. III

#### The handbook

[The handbook](https://creed.apps.wayne.edu/handbook/) has the rules, one chapter per topic, and each rule links the decision behind it. Where we haven't decided yet, the chapter says "To be decided" and gives no rule.

Form CR-1 · Field inspection

### Inspect a version

Pick a runtime, a version and a day. The form uses the same dates and rules as `Policy::stateOf`: a version is still supported on its last day, then it gets 90 days of grace. After that, no override helps. The inspector stamps what he finds.

Certificate of inspection

No. 0001

- **Runtime**: PHP 8.2
- **Inspected on**: 2026-10-29
- **Reader call**: `$policy->stateOf('php', '8.2', new DateTimeImmutable('2026-10-29'))`
- **Returns**: `State::Security`

Security fixes only, until 2026-12-31: 63 days left. Plan the move to PHP 8.4 now.

Applicable clause: [§2.2 Treat security-only as a countdown, not a resting place](https://creed.apps.wayne.edu/#c-2-2)

Inspector CREED reader, schema v1

Chapter 1

### The version policy as data

Creed Bratton keeps his own records and nobody can audit them. CREED does the opposite: every date is in one file, with a source, where anyone can check it.

#### §1.1 Keep one machine-readable policy, and let one reader decide state.

Every tool reads `policy.json` through the CREED reader. No other code decides whether a version is active, security-only or EOL.

Held by `Waynestate\Creed\Policy`, the only implementation. [PROCTOR](https://creed.apps.wayne.edu/#ahj-proctor), Booster and Rollcall each carry a generated copy, and `bin/export.php --check` fails when a copy drifts.

Documented

**Rationale.** Two tools with two copies of a date will eventually disagree, and a developer cannot tell which to believe.

#### §1.2 Validate the policy file against a schema in CI.

A bad date, a wrong type or an unknown key fails the build.

Held by `PolicySchemaTest` and `composer validate-policy`, both in [Preflight](https://creed.apps.wayne.edu/#ahj-preflight) `php-test`.

Enforced

**Rationale.** A typo in a date silently changes what every tool reports.

#### §1.4 Make the reader refuse to guess.

A version with no `security_until` is an error, not a silent pass, unless its line is marked current. An unknown component, or a version between the listed lines, is an error. A version older than the oldest listed line is EOL. A version newer than every listed line is Active: current versions are never refused.

Held by `stateOf`, which throws for each error case, and `isAheadOfPolicy`; tests cover every one.

Enforced

**Rationale.** A tool that guesses turns missing data into a green check.

#### §1.5 Compute state from the date, with an inclusive end and a stated grace period.

A version is still supported on its `security_until` day. It is EOL the next day. After `eol_grace_days` (90) it is past grace, and no override applies.

Held by `PolicyStateTest`, on the PHP 8.2 boundary days.

Enforced

**Rationale.** Everyone must get the same answer on the same day, including on the boundary. *With arms wide open*: the window stays open through the last day.

#### §1.9 Model support honestly when a project publishes no dates.

Vue 3 and Inertia publish no fixed end dates. Do not invent them. The policy marks Vue 3, Inertia 2 and Inertia 3 `"current": true`: Active on every date, with no `security_until`. Vue 2 keeps its real end, 2023-12-31.

Held by the schema, which refuses a current line that carries `security_until` and a dated line without it; `PolicySchemaTest` covers both.

Enforced

**Rationale.** A made-up date is worse than an honest "no date".

Chapter 2

### PHP and framework versions

EOL PHP is not supported by the stack, with no exceptions. The adopted editions are in Table 2-1.

#### §2.1 Run non-EOL PHP only.

Apps declare and run a PHP version that php.net lists as supported. On 2026-10-29 that means 8.2 (security only, to 2026-12-31), 8.3, 8.4 and 8.5.

Held by [PROCTOR](https://creed.apps.wayne.edu/#ahj-proctor) `php-floor`, which fails when the lowest bound of `require.php` is EOL by policy.

Checked

**Rationale.** An EOL branch receives no security fixes.

#### §2.2 Treat security-only as a countdown, not a resting place.

A version in security-only support warns now and fails on the day after `security_until`. Plan the move before then.

Held by [PROCTOR](https://creed.apps.wayne.edu/#ahj-proctor) `php-floor` (a WARN). [HELMET](https://creed.apps.wayne.edu/#ahj-helmet) ships the runtime ribbon.

Checked

**Rationale.** Moving on a deadline day is how upgrades go wrong.

#### §2.3 Raise the floor on the day the old version ends.

The PHP floor for apps moves from `^8.2` to `^8.3` on 2027-01-01. CREED itself already requires `^8.3`; Creed has always been one version ahead of everyone else, at least by his own account.

Held by `oldestSupported` computes it. No automation bumps a package's constraint.

Documented

**Rationale.** It is the only way a dependency floor can force an upgrade.

Table 2-1 Adopted editions, with the state on 2026-10-29

| Runtime | Active until | Security until | Latest patch | State |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| PHP floor **8.2** |  |  |  |  |
| 8.5 | 2027-12-31 | 2029-12-31 | 8.5.12 | Active |
| 8.4 | 2026-12-31 | 2028-12-31 | 8.4.27 | Active |
| 8.3 | 2025-12-31 | 2027-12-31 | 8.3.36 | Security |
| 8.2 | 2024-12-31 | 2026-12-31 | 8.2.35 | Security |
| 8.1 | 2023-11-25 | 2025-12-31 | n/a | Grace expired |
| Laravel floor **12** |  |  |  |  |
| 13 | 2027-09-30 | 2028-03-17 | 13.39.0 | Active |
| 12 | 2026-08-13 | 2027-02-24 | 12.70.2 | Security |
| 11 | 2025-09-03 | 2026-03-12 | 11.57.1 | Grace expired |
| 10 | 2024-08-06 | 2025-02-04 | 10.50.4 | Grace expired |
| Node floor **22** |  |  |  |  |
| 26 | 2027-10-20 | 2029-04-30 | 26.13.0 | Active |
| 24 | 2026-10-20 | 2028-04-30 | 24.22.2 | Security |
| 22 | 2025-10-21 | 2027-04-30 | 22.23.4 | Security |
| 20 | 2024-10-22 | 2026-04-30 | 20.20.2 | Grace expired |
| MySQL floor **8.4** |  |  |  |  |
| 9.7 | 2031-04-30 | 2034-04-30 | n/a | Active |
| 8.4 | 2029-04-30 | 2032-04-30 | n/a | Active |
| 8.0 | 2025-04-30 | 2026-04-30 | n/a | Grace expired |
| 5.7 | 2020-10-31 | 2023-10-31 | n/a | Grace expired |
| 5.6 | 2018-02-28 | 2021-02-28 | n/a | Grace expired |
| Vue and Inertia |  |  |  |  |
| Vue 2 | 2023-12-31 | 2023-12-31 | n/a | Grace expired |
| Vue 3 | Current line: no published end dates, none invented; see §1.9. | Active |  |  |
| Inertia 2 | Current line: no published end dates, none invented; see §1.9. | Active |  |  |
| Inertia 3 | Current line: no published end dates, none invented; see §1.9. | Active |  |  |

From `policy/policy.json`, schema version 1, patches checked 2026-10-28 and 2026-10-29. For Node, "active" holds the maintenance start; for MySQL, the Premier end. That mapping is the policy's, not the vendors' wording.

#### §2.5 Run a Laravel release that still gets security fixes.

Laravel gives bug fixes for 18 months and security fixes for two years. Laravel 11 and older are EOL. Laravel 12 gets security fixes until 2027-02-24; Laravel 13 until 2028-03-17.

Held by The reader can classify 10 to 13. PROCTOR `unpatched` reads `laravel/framework` from `composer.lock` and warns when the locked patch trails the policy's `latest_patch`; PROCTOR main's `proctor/laravel-eol` classifies the locked Laravel line through the policy, where an active line passes, a security-only line warns and an EOL line fails.

Checked

**Rationale.** An EOL framework is the largest unpatched surface in a typical app.

#### §2.6 Use a Node release that is in LTS or maintenance.

Build front ends on a Node line that has not reached end of life: 22, 24 and 26. Node 20 reached end of life on 2026-04-30.

Held by The dates are in `policy.json`. PROCTOR main's `proctor/node-eol` reads the Node version an app pins in `.nvmrc`, `volta.node`, CI and Dockerfiles, and grades it through the policy: an active line passes, a security-only line warns and an EOL line fails.

Checked

**Rationale.** Build tools run with your credentials and your source.

#### §2.7 Choose a supported MySQL, and say when the platform lags.

MySQL 8.4 LTS has Premier support to 2029-04-30 and Extended to 2032-04-30. MySQL 8.0 ended on 2026-04-30 and is past CREED's 90-day grace since 2026-07-29.

Gap Nothing checks it, and the platform's own MySQL timeline is still an open question.

Not yet

**Rationale.** A database that no longer gets fixes holds everything above it back.

Chapter 3

### Dependencies

What goes into an app, and how it is allowed in.

#### §3.1 Commit the lock file.

`composer.lock` is in the repository for apps. Use `composer install` in CI and on deploy, not `composer update`.

Held by [PROCTOR](https://creed.apps.wayne.edu/#ahj-proctor) `lock-committed`.

Checked

**Rationale.** Without a lock, a build next week is a different build.

#### §3.2 Ban open-ended constraints.

No `dev-*` branches and no `*` on runtime dependencies. Use caret constraints such as `^2.4`.

Held by [PROCTOR](https://creed.apps.wayne.edu/#ahj-proctor) `unbounded-constraints`, using `banned_constraints` from the policy.

Checked

**Rationale.** An open constraint lets an unreviewed change into production.

#### §3.3 Audit dependencies and fail at a stated severity.

Run `composer audit --locked` in CI and fail at or above the policy threshold, `high`.

Held by [Preflight](https://creed.apps.wayne.edu/#ahj-preflight) `composer-audit` and [PROCTOR](https://creed.apps.wayne.edu/#ahj-proctor) `composer-audit`.

Checked

**Rationale.** Known advisories are the cheapest attacks to run.

#### §3.6 Pin CI components to a tag or SHA.

Include shared CI components at a tag or a full commit SHA, never `~latest`. CREED's own pipeline pins both of its components to a SHA.

Held by `ci.md`; components from [Preflight](https://creed.apps.wayne.edu/#ahj-preflight). No check scans other repos.

Documented

**Rationale.** A moving reference lets an upstream change weaken your pipeline without a commit in your repo.

Chapter 4

### Secrets and configuration

Of the three practices in this chapter, one is checked, one is partly checked and one is written down only. The last two are printed below.

#### §4.1 Keep secrets out of source control.

Do not commit `.env`, keys, tokens or passwords. Commit `.env.example` with placeholders. Rotate a secret that was ever exposed.

Gap The handbook's secrets chapter writes the rules. PROCTOR main warns on a committed `.env` or `APP_KEY` (`proctor/app-key`) and on a token in a package source URL (`proctor/repo-url-credentials`); no general secret scan exists yet.

Partially

**Rationale.** A repository is copied to many machines and outlives any one password.

#### §4.3 Never run production with debug on.

`APP_DEBUG` is `false` in production.

Held by The handbook's runtime and headers and secrets chapters. [HELMET](https://creed.apps.wayne.edu/#ahj-helmet) warns when a Laravel app boots with debug on in production; no PROCTOR check reads `APP_DEBUG` yet.

Documented

**Rationale.** Debug pages expose configuration values to users.

Chapter 5

### Overrides and rollout

Every code has variances. These are the rules for asking for one.

#### §5.1 Make every exception named, dated and visible.

An override sits in the app's `policy-overrides.json` with a reason and an expiry. Every run prints every override. An expired override fails.

Held by [PROCTOR](https://creed.apps.wayne.edu/#ahj-proctor) `overrides`. [Rollcall](https://creed.apps.wayne.edu/#ahj-rollcall) counts expired overrides across apps in its fleet report.

Checked

**Rationale.** An exception without an end date becomes the rule.

#### §5.2 Roll a new rule out in stages, with dates.

Each rule moves `report`, then `warn`, then `block`. A deploy that does not make things worse always passes.

Held by the proposed deploy gate. The schema has no field for stage dates yet.

Documented

**Rationale.** Blocking every non-compliant app on day one blocks the fixes too.

Chapter 6

### Writing the handbook

The rules for writing CREED itself. Mostly: link the decision, and don't let a gate depend on anyone's opinion.

#### §6.1 Cite the decision behind every rule.

Each handbook rule links to the ADR that decided it. Where nothing is decided, the chapter says "To be decided" and states no rule.

Documented

**Rationale.** Readers can trust a rule, and can find who to ask about the rest.

#### §6.4 Judge with deterministic checks only.

No gate depends on a language model's opinion. A model may explain a failure; it does not decide pass or fail.

Documented

**Rationale.** A gate must give the same answer twice.

#### §6.5 Keep every developer tool usable on Windows, macOS and Linux.

Scripts ship as a `.ps1` and `.sh` pair, or as one PHP command. Every repo carries `.gitattributes` with `* text=auto eol=lf`.

Documented

**Rationale.** Developers work on all three, and the servers need LF.

#### §6.6 Run the test suite on every supported PHP version.

CI runs CREED's unit tests on 8.3, 8.4 and 8.5, from its own floor up.

Held by [Preflight](https://creed.apps.wayne.edu/#ahj-preflight) `php-test`, a matrix in CREED's pipeline.

Checked

**Rationale.** A library that works only on the newest PHP excludes half its users.

Chapter 7 · Added in the second pass

### Patching and the supply chain

Nine practices, two checked so far. Chapters 8 to 11 (platform and database, policy data, accessibility, and the WSU developer standards of 2024) are in the book, with their stamps in the contents.

#### §7.1 Track the PHP patch release, not only the branch.

A supported branch is not a patched one. On 2026-10-21 PHP released 8.5.12, 8.4.27, 8.3.36 and 8.2.35 to fix two critical advisories. `policy.json` now carries a `latest_patch` for each branch.

Held by `latestPatch()` in the reader; maintainers refresh it with `php bin/refresh-patches.php`.

Documented

**Rationale.** The branch tells you whether fixes still come; the patch tells you whether you took them.

Inserted after printing

### Errata and pending amendments

The questions the 2026 edition hasn't answered. Each one names the clause it affects. It stays open until we make a decision or find a source.

| No. | Clause | Erratum or amendment | Status |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| E-4 | §9.3 | Strict or tolerant schema: can an older tool still read a newer policy that only added a field? A test with an old schema and reader decides. | Open |
| E-5 | §9.1 | Node 27 and later have no Maintenance phase on the new yearly schedule, so how `active_until` is derived needs a new rule. | Open |
| E-6 | Ch. 10 | The accessibility chapter: aim at WCAG 2.2 AA, after confirming which legal dates apply. To be decided. | Open |
| E-7 | Handbook | Runtime and headers: no rules until a decision lands with HELMET. The auth chapter still has the gateway's key distribution, and the SAML library if a SAML driver is built, to decide. | Open |

The full backlog, 37 items, is at the end of [BEST_PRACTICES.md](https://github.com/waynestate/creed/blob/main/BEST_PRACTICES.md#gaps-for-the-backlog).

Appendix A

### Adopting this code

Two ways in: read the policy from your own PHP tool, or clone CREED and run its checks.

#### A.1 Read the policy from PHP

Any OS with PHP 8.3 or newer and Composer. On Packagist, 0.1.3

`$ composer require waynestate/creed`

```
use Waynestate\Creed\Policy;
use Waynestate\Creed\State;

$policy = Policy::bundled();

// What state is PHP 8.2 in, on this date?
$state = $policy->stateOf('php', '8.2', new DateTimeImmutable('2026-10-27'));
// State::Security

// What is the oldest PHP an app may declare?
$floor = $policy->oldestSupported('php', new DateTimeImmutable('2026-10-27'));
// '8.2'
```

#### A.2 Run CREED's checks

In a clone with PHP and Composer, this runs every check: `composer validate`, PHPUnit, the policy schema, Pint, the handbook lint, the site staleness checks, PHPStan and `composer audit`. GitLab and GitHub run the same command.

`$ composer ci`

No PHP on your machine? Docker can run the tests and the schema check.

**Windows**

PowerShell, with Docker Desktop.

```
PS> docker run --rm -v "${PWD}:/app" -w /app composer:2.10.3 composer install --no-interaction
PS> docker run --rm -v "${PWD}:/app" -w /app php:8.4-cli vendor/bin/phpunit
PS> docker run --rm -v "${PWD}:/app" -w /app composer:2.10.3 composer validate-policy
```

**macOS**

Terminal, with Docker Desktop.

```
$ docker run --rm -v "${PWD}:/app" -w /app composer:2.10.3 composer install --no-interaction
$ docker run --rm -v "${PWD}:/app" -w /app php:8.4-cli vendor/bin/phpunit
$ docker run --rm -v "${PWD}:/app" -w /app composer:2.10.3 composer validate-policy
```

**Linux**

Any shell, with Docker Engine.

```
$ docker run --rm -v "${PWD}:/app" -w /app composer:2.10.3 composer install --no-interaction
$ docker run --rm -v "${PWD}:/app" -w /app php:8.4-cli vendor/bin/phpunit
$ docker run --rm -v "${PWD}:/app" -w /app composer:2.10.3 composer validate-policy
```

Maintainers: to pull new patch numbers from the upstream feeds, run `php bin/refresh-patches.php --dry-run` (drop `--dry-run` to write).

**Strongly recommended:** a git.wayne.edu instance runner. CI is a gate only if something runs it (§6.7), and git.wayne.edu has no runners today.

Appendix B

### Hand it to your agent

Four prompts for whatever coding agent you use. Copy one, or open it in OpenCode, Claude Code, Codex or ChatGPT. Each tells the agent where CREED's pages are and what it must not assume, and all four tell it to ask you before it guesses.

#### Get started with CREED

Lists every version your app runs with its state today, then proposes the smallest change that fixes anything past end of life. It won't make the change until you say so.

A prompt for your coding agent. Copy it as it stands:

```text
You are a coding agent helping a Wayne State University developer bring the app in this folder up to CREED, the written standard of WELD, the Wayne State application stack. CREED is two things: policy.json, the support dates for PHP, Laravel, Node, MySQL, Vue and Inertia, and a handbook of numbered practices.

Read first:
- https://creed.apps.wayne.edu/llms.txt, the index of CREED's pages, each one as Markdown. Fetch the pages you need; do not work from memory.
- This app's composer.json and composer.lock, and package.json with its lock file if there is one.
- ADVISOR, the stack's MCP server, if it is connected: its policy_lookup and list_stack_rules tools answer from CREED, with the date and the source. If it is not connected, say so and work from the pages. How to add it: https://advisor.apps.wayne.edu/llms.txt

Task:
1. Say which kind of app this is: raw PHP, raw PHP with Vue, Laravel with Blade, Laravel with Blade and Vue, or Laravel with Inertia and Vue.
2. List every version it declares or locks: the PHP floor, Laravel, Node, Vue, Inertia, and MySQL if you can tell.
3. For each one, give the state CREED assigns it today (Active, Security, Eol or EolGraceExpired), the date that state ends, and the clause that applies.
4. Propose the smallest change that moves anything past end of life onto a supported line. Do not make it yet.

Constraints:
- CREED decides a version's state. Never guess a date: read it from the policy or from ADVISOR, and say which.
- An app that reads the policy itself installs the reader with `composer require waynestate/creed`. Never copy policy.json into the app.
- Give separate commands for Windows (PowerShell), macOS and Linux wherever they differ.
- Ask me before you guess: a version you cannot read, an app kind you cannot tell, or anything that touches a deploy.

Output: a table (component, version, state, until, clause), then the change as numbered steps, then your questions.
```

#### Or start from your consumer path

#### CREED in a raw PHP app

Checks an app with no framework against the rules that apply to it, and cites a file and line for each result.

A prompt for your coding agent. Copy it as it stands:

```text
You are a coding agent reviewing a raw PHP app (no framework) at Wayne State University against CREED, the written standard of WELD, the Wayne State application stack.

Read first:
- https://creed.apps.wayne.edu/llms.txt, then the handbook chapters it lists. Every rule there cites the decision behind it.
- ADVISOR, the stack's MCP server, if it is connected: call list_stack_rules with permutation raw-php (raw-php-vue if the app builds Vue), and policy_lookup for each runtime. If it is not connected, say so and work from the handbook pages.
- composer.json, composer.lock, the entry scripts or front controller, and any CI file.

Task:
1. Check the app against the rules that apply to raw PHP: versions, dependencies, secrets and configuration, runtime and headers, auth, and CI.
2. For each rule, record Pass, Fail or Cannot tell, with the file and line that shows it.
3. Change nothing yet. Propose the three fixes that buy the most, smallest first.

Constraints:
- Cite the chapter and rule for every finding: the handbook file and line from ADVISOR, or the page URL.
- A raw PHP app has no framework to lean on. Say what the app itself must do, and never suggest adding Laravel just to meet a rule.
- The PHP floor comes from the policy, not from memory.
- Ask me before you guess, and before you touch anything that deploys.

Output: a findings table (rule, chapter, result, evidence), then the three fixes, then your questions.
```

#### CREED in a Laravel app with Blade

The same review for Laravel with Blade. It looks at config, middleware and the Laravel line.

A prompt for your coding agent. Copy it as it stands:

```text
You are a coding agent reviewing a Laravel app that renders its pages with Blade, at Wayne State University, against CREED, the written standard of WELD, the Wayne State application stack.

Read first:
- https://creed.apps.wayne.edu/llms.txt, then the handbook chapters it lists. Every rule there cites the decision behind it.
- ADVISOR, the stack's MCP server, if it is connected: call list_stack_rules with permutation laravel-blade (laravel-blade-vue if Blade pages mount Vue components), and policy_lookup for PHP and Laravel. If it is not connected, say so and work from the handbook pages.
- composer.json, composer.lock, config/, bootstrap/app.php, .env.example, and any CI file.

Task:
1. Check the app against the rules that apply to Laravel with Blade: the PHP floor and the Laravel line, dependencies, secrets and .env, runtime and headers, auth, and CI.
2. For each rule, record Pass, Fail or Cannot tell, with the file and line that shows it.
3. Change nothing yet. Propose the three fixes that buy the most, smallest first.

Constraints:
- Cite the chapter and rule for every finding: the handbook file and line from ADVISOR, or the page URL.
- Meet a rule the Laravel way (config, middleware, a service provider) before writing code of your own.
- Laravel's support dates come from CREED's policy, not from memory or from laravel.com.
- Ask me before you guess, and before you touch migrations or anything that deploys.

Output: a findings table (rule, chapter, result, evidence), then the three fixes, then your questions.
```

#### CREED in a Laravel app with Inertia and Vue

Reviews the Composer side and the npm side, including Node, Vue and Inertia. A missing npm lock file counts as a finding.

A prompt for your coding agent. Copy it as it stands:

```text
You are a coding agent reviewing a Laravel app with Inertia and Vue, at Wayne State University, against CREED, the written standard of WELD, the Wayne State application stack. It has two halves, and CREED covers both.

Read first:
- https://creed.apps.wayne.edu/llms.txt, then the handbook chapters it lists. Every rule there cites the decision behind it.
- ADVISOR, the stack's MCP server, if it is connected: call list_stack_rules with permutation laravel-inertia-vue, and policy_lookup for PHP, Laravel, Node, Vue and Inertia. If it is not connected, say so and work from the handbook pages.
- The PHP half: composer.json, composer.lock, config/, .env.example. The frontend half: package.json, its lock file, .npmrc, the Vite config. And any CI file.

Task:
1. Check the app against the rules that apply to Laravel with Inertia and Vue: the PHP, Laravel, Node, Vue and Inertia lines, dependencies on both sides, secrets and .env, runtime and headers, auth, and CI.
2. For each rule, record Pass, Fail or Cannot tell, with the file and line that shows it.
3. Change nothing yet. Propose the three fixes that buy the most, smallest first.

Constraints:
- Cite the chapter and rule for every finding: the handbook file and line from ADVISOR, or the page URL.
- The npm side counts as much as the Composer side: a missing or uncommitted lock file is a finding.
- Every support date comes from CREED's policy, never from memory.
- Ask me before you guess, and before you touch migrations, the build, or anything that deploys.

Output: a findings table (rule, chapter, result, evidence, half), then the three fixes, then your questions.
```

The agent reads the same pages you do: [llms.txt](https://creed.apps.wayne.edu/llms.txt) lists them, [llms-full.txt](https://creed.apps.wayne.edu/llms-full.txt) holds them all in one file, and every page has a Markdown twin. Nothing here phones home. The buttons only copy text or open the tool you picked.

## Changelog[#](https://creed.apps.wayne.edu/docs/changelog.html#changelog)

### Unreleased[#](https://creed.apps.wayne.edu/docs/changelog.html#unreleased)

- Docs: the handbook writes Rollcall as a word, not in capitals.
- Fixed: the pipeline's PROCTOR jobs no longer pass `--policy`, which PROCTOR 0.7 refuses in CI; PROCTOR checks against the CREED policy it bundles.
- Changed: the GitLab pipeline pins the Preflight components to 0.2.0 (was 0.1.4).
- Changed: the front page's deploy layer (`deploy/`) runs Squire's kit 0.6.0 (was 0.5.0): `scripts/release.sh` asks PROCTOR's deploy gate for a go or no-go on each release (a report, not a stop, unless `SQUIRE_PROCTOR=enforce`), and `.env.squire.example` lists the new setting. The layer pins HELMET `^0.4` (locked 0.4.0).
- Fixed: the front page's authorities table says Sourdough starts all five app shapes, from raw PHP to Inertia and Vue; it no longer says raw PHP only.
- Changed: the front-page deploy layer pins PROCTOR ^0.7 (lock: PROCTOR 0.7.0, was 0.4.0).
- Changed: CI caches Composer downloads per lock file (`.composer-cache`, keyed on `composer.lock` and `deploy/composer.lock`), so a pipeline stops fetching every package from Packagist on every run. Images already come through the Dependency Proxy.

### 0.1.7 (2026-11-07)[#](https://creed.apps.wayne.edu/docs/changelog.html#0-1-7-2026-11-07)

- Changed: the front page's deploy layer (`deploy/`) runs Squire's kit 0.5.0 (was 0.3.4): `oracle-check.php` arrives, `scripts/release.sh` and `scripts/parity.ps1` take the new templates, and the two kit files Renovate had edited (`docker-compose.squire.yml`, `.squire/base-fallback.Dockerfile`, which it had moved to PHP 8.5) are Squire's template again, so `squire init --check` passes. The shared Renovate preset leaves kit files alone now. `site/assets/stack-env.js` takes the stack's one copy, with bindingless catch blocks.
- Changed: The canonical repository is git.wayne.edu (ADR-0021); docs, links and package metadata no longer point at the archived nougat copy.
- Changed: practices 16, 25 and 43 move to Checked, and 59 moves from Not yet to Partially, held by five new checks on PROCTOR main: `node-eol` (the Node line an app pins), `env-outside-config`, `app-key` (a committed `.env` or `APP_KEY`, and the cookie session driver), `served-folder` and `world-writable`. Practices 24 and 55 move from Documented to Partially for the same checks. The tally is now Enforced 7, Checked 14, Partially 9, Documented 22, Not yet 9; the front page's chapter bars and clauses 2.6 and 4.1, the backlog, and the handbook's versions, code, secrets and production chapters name the checks, and the secrets chapter gains an `APP_KEY` rule (rotate a leaked key, no cookie sessions).
- Fixed: the front page's citation links (the clause numbers beside each stack part in the authorities table) are at least 24 px wide and tall, meeting the WCAG 2.5.8 target size at 320 px in light and dark.
- Changed: Practices 14, 15 and 21 move to Checked: PROCTOR's laravel-php, laravel-eol and composer-audit abandoned checks enforce them.
- Changed: the handbook walk reaches the last five chapters (code, runtime-and-headers, secrets, production, deploy-gate): every MUST and SHOULD rule now names its point, a PROCTOR check ID, a measuring command, or the plain words "no check exists yet"; practices 29 and 32 record the completed walk and what remains, and the site's handbook pages and search index are regenerated.
- Changed: practice 39 is stamped Checked: PROCTOR's `composer-version` check fails a Composer below the higher of its CVE floors and CREED's policy minimum (`tools.composer.minimum`, 2.8.0), and the best-practices intro now names the Preflight 0.1.4 pin CI runs; the front page's tally and chapter 7 bar follow.
- Changed: nine stale stamps re-checked against the tree (2026-11-06): practices 14, 39, 44 and 46 move to Partially, 24, 42 and 49 to Documented, 51 to Enforced, and 50 stays Partially with its pipeline fact corrected; the front page's tally, chapter bars and section 4.1 clause follow, its Docker quickstart pins composer:2.10.3 like the README, and two cross-references plus four backlog lines that contradicted the new record are fixed.
- Added: a site accessibility gate (axe-core in Playwright, WCAG 2.2 AA, run in Docker): `scripts/a11y.sh` on Linux and macOS, `scripts/a11y.ps1` on Windows; it checks the front page, every docs page and every handbook page in light and dark at 360 and 1280 px.
- Added: the abandoned-package rule (`rules.abandoned_packages`: ignore, report or fail, `fail` in the bundled policy) to the policy, schema and reader, with the handbook decision next to the audit rule.
- Fixed: the refresh command's tests use a frozen policy snapshot, so the policy robot's refresh merge requests no longer fail them.
- Fixed: the front page's contents and key now tell the same story as the tally. Every chapter's stamp bar is recounted from BEST_PRACTICES.md, chapter 11 (WSU developer standards) has its row, the key explains all five stamps, and the new Partially stamp has its own ink (moss, between Checked's ochre and Documented's slate), a half-dashed frame and hatched bars. §4.3 is stamped Documented as BEST_PRACTICES.md has it, and the chapter 4 and 7 introductions say so. BEST_PRACTICES.md's own key lists Partially.
- Added: `FrontPageTallyTest` fails `composer ci` when the front page's tally, contents heading, chapter bars, clause ranges, key or reprinted clause stamps drift from BEST_PRACTICES.md.
- Fixed: the front page tally matches BEST_PRACTICES.md again: eleven chapters, 61 practices, and the stamps recounted (Enforced 6, Checked 7, Partially 4, Documented 21, Not yet 23); the README screenshot alt text states no counts.
- Fixed: the policy robot's nothing-staged line prints a real newline instead of a literal backslash-n, and the refresher's exit 4 comment says what the robot really does: it commits whatever else the run wrote (often nothing) and pushes the merge request without auto-merge.
- Changed: the docs' dark mode is the code book read after hours (warm graphite stock, cream type, a pale tint of the green ink for links, gold foil for the title rule, the current page and focus) instead of a green wallpaper; every kit dark token is set by the theme. The cover's gold ribbon marks the page you are reading and each callout's stamp is pressed as it scrolls in (motion only under prefers-reduced-motion: no-preference); stamp frames wear the front page's ink texture; wide tables shade the side that scrolls.
- Fixed: the docs and README describe the policy robot as it runs: the Monday schedule, the four outcomes, the merge request (title, label, auto-merge only after exit 3, force-pushed branch), the auto-alert issues, how to review a robot merge request, and the setup. Support dates are no longer described as hand-edited only, refresher exit 4 no longer says nothing is committed, and the composer ci lists name every step.

On phones the running head sets like the docs (name over menu, two lines of three links, not sticky); the menu now hides Errata as intended instead of Inspect; the title-page book leaves room for its tabs in a narrow column.
- Added: per-Laravel-line `requires` (PHP range, MySQL and MariaDB minimums) in the policy, schema and reader.

### 0.1.3 (2026-10-29)[#](https://creed.apps.wayne.edu/docs/changelog.html#0-1-3-2026-10-29)

- Changed: the proof page moves to a private site that needs a Wayne State sign-in.
- Changed: project names written as words except acronyms.
- Changed: README images show the current site and policy.
- Changed: README names which tools carry the reader copy; the auth chapter lists the `oidc` driver.
- Changed: the agent-ready kit is Squire 0.3.0's, so generated labels read "Squire's agent-ready kit".
- `bin/policy-bot.php run`: a real (non dry-run) run now commits the data allowlist on `auto/policy-refresh` and force-pushes it with GitLab merge request push options (create, target, remove source branch, label `auto-data`, title; `merge_request.auto_merge` on exit 3 only). The push URL comes from the CI_SERVER\_\* variables and CREED_BOT_TOKEN; missing variables stop the run with exit 1 naming them, and every printed line masks the token as `[masked]`. After an exit 0, a refresh whose `refreshed_on` is 7 or more days old runs the refresher again with `--touch` and treats that result like a normal run.
- `bin/policy-bot.php run`: after a handled real run the robot now keeps its GitLab alert issues in line with the report, one open issue per alert key (`held:<component>:<line>:<field>`, `refused:<component>:<line>:<field>`, `disagreement:<component>:<line>:<field>` while policy sides with neither source, and `upcoming-eol:<component>:<line>` within 60 days of `security_until`), each labelled `auto-alert` and titled `[auto-alert] <key>`. A key that is still present gets a note on its existing issue; a key that is gone is closed with a "Cleared on ." note. The client is built from CI_API_V4_URL, CI_PROJECT_ID and CREED_BOT_TOKEN; an incomplete environment stops the run with exit 1 naming the missing variables. A dry run prints the issues it would open and never calls the API.
- New `src/Bot/GitLabClient.php`: a small GitLab API client (list open issues, create an issue, add a note, close an issue) over an injectable `HttpTransport`, shipped with a dependency-free PHP streams transport (`GitLabClient::streamTransport`). The token rides only in the `PRIVATE-TOKEN` header, never in a URL, and every error it throws is masked, so a failed call can never print the token.
- Fixed: stale capability claims in the site and docs.

### 0.1.2 (2026-10-29)[#](https://creed.apps.wayne.edu/docs/changelog.html#0-1-2-2026-10-29)

- `bin/refresh-policy.php`: a released version that loosens a constraint now exits 3 (changes written) with an alert in the report, instead of exit 4.
- Fixed: a version of a known component that is older than the oldest listed line (PHP 5.x to 8.0, Laravel 5 to 8, Inertia 0.x) is now `Eol`, with the reason `older than the oldest listed line (8.1)` from the new `belowOldestLineReason($component, $version)`, instead of being refused as an unknown version. Unlisted components and version strings that do not parse are still refused, and a version above every listed line is still `Active`.

### 0.1.1 (2026-10-29)[#](https://creed.apps.wayne.edu/docs/changelog.html#0-1-1-2026-10-29)

- `bin/refresh-policy.php` keeps every support date, patch and new line in the policy tied to a canonical source (php.net, the Node.js release schedule, endoflife.date, Packagist, npm). Changes are classed tighten, neutral, loosen-warning or loosen-fail; a later security date is held until two sources agree or 14 days pass; nothing is ever removed. Provenance lives in the new `policy/sources.json` (schema and validation included), and the policy gains an optional `refreshed_on` date. `refresh-patches.php` keeps working.
- PHPStan now includes Pinstripe's raw preset (`vendor/waynestate/pinstripe/phpstan/raw.neon`) instead of carrying a hand copy; `phpstan.neon` keeps only this repo's own paths and phpVersion. `waynestate/pinstripe` joins require-dev (dev-main until 0.1.0 is tagged) and `phpstan/extension-installer` is allowed so the preset's deprecation rules load. The suit is off the rack now.
- `handbook/dependencies.md` gains a "Private packages" section: internal-only packages install from one GitLab registry per ecosystem, credentials stay out of repository URLs and lock files, builds use read-only deploy tokens, the private Composer entry is canonical, released versions never move, and public code goes to Packagist or npm. PROCTOR checks and the PREFLIGHT publish job enforce the rules. One standard, no cover versions.
- Policy lines may be marked `"current": true`: Active on every date, with no `security_until`. The schema rejects a current line that also carries a `security_until`, and a line that carries neither.
- `stateOf()` resolves a version to its policy line before judging it. A version that sorts above every listed line is `Active` (current versions are never refused), while a version between listed lines still throws.
- New reader method `isAheadOfPolicy($component, $version)`.
- `line()` reports a fifth field, `current` (true or null).
- The bundled policy lists Vue 3 and Inertia 2 as current lines.
- `bin/refresh-patches.php` reads the endoflife.date Vue feed and proposes new Vue lines (a current line, or EOL dates) alongside the patch refresh.
- The README's reader example is now a test: `tests/ReadmeTest.php` runs every
  ```php
  values printed beside it. A snippet that cannot run as-is is skipped with a
  `<!-- readme-test: skip -->` comment.
  ```
- The handbook is now linted for RFC 2119 capitalization. `src/HandbookLinter.php` and `bin/lint-handbook.php` flag lowercase `must`, `must not`, `should`, `should not` and `may` in any chapter that declares RFC 2119, ignoring code spans and blocks; a same-line `<!-- lint: allow -->` excuses a deliberate plain-English use. `composer ci` runs the lint as `lint-handbook`.
- Every handbook chapter now declares RFC 2119 and uses capital keywords; `handbook/databases.md` gains a "Grace period" section spelling out the 90-day `eol_grace_days` window (`Security` on `security_until`, `Eol` for the window, `EolGraceExpired` after, no override).

## Contributing[#](https://creed.apps.wayne.edu/docs/contributing.html#contributing)

This page tells you how to build, test and release CREED, and how its policy data stays current.

### Where the code lives[#](https://creed.apps.wayne.edu/docs/contributing.html#where-the-code-lives)

Development happens on git.wayne.edu, the canonical repository ([enterprise-apps/creed](https://git.wayne.edu/enterprise-apps/creed)). GitHub ([waynestate/creed](https://github.com/waynestate/creed)) is a read-only push mirror: `main` and tags are copied automatically, and Packagist picks releases up from it. Changes, issues and merge requests go to git.wayne.edu; tags are made there, by the maintainer, with an approver. Nobody pushes to the mirror.

### Build and test[#](https://creed.apps.wayne.edu/docs/contributing.html#build-and-test)

You need PHP 8.3 or newer and Composer, or only Docker. Everything has a native path on Windows (PowerShell), Linux and macOS.

| Task | Command |
| --- | --- |
| Install | `composer install` |
| All checks (what CI runs) | `composer ci` |
| Only the tests | `composer test` |
| Validate `policy.json` against its schema | `composer validate-policy` |
| Lint the handbook | `composer lint-handbook` |
| Fix code style | `composer fix` |

With only Docker (the same line works in PowerShell and sh):

```sh
docker run --rm -v "${PWD}:/app" -w /app composer:2.10.3 sh -c "composer install --no-interaction && composer ci"
docker run --rm -v "${PWD}:/app" -w /app php:8.5-cli vendor/bin/phpunit
```

`composer ci` runs `composer validate --strict`, the tests, the policy validator, Pint, the handbook lint, the handbook site and agent-ready freshness checks, PHPStan, `composer audit` and the docs site freshness check. On Windows, if tests fail oddly after a Docker install, delete `vendor/` and install again.

### The docs site[#](https://creed.apps.wayne.edu/docs/contributing.html#the-docs-site)

The documentation site is built by `composer docs` and checked by `composer docs:check`. Its sources live in `docs/`, one Markdown file per page, and `composer ci` fails when the committed pages go stale.

### CI[#](https://creed.apps.wayne.edu/docs/contributing.html#ci)

- **GitLab:** Preflight components (`php-test` on PHP 8.3, 8.4 and 8.5, `composer-audit`, and `proctor` for the `deploy/` layer), plus a `composer-ci` job and a `wayneui-copies` job. On scheduled pipelines, `refresh-patches` (check-only) runs on a schedule without `CREED_JOB`, and `policy-bot` runs on the Monday schedule that carries `CREED_JOB=policy-bot` (and by hand from the web).
- **GitHub:** `.github/workflows/ci.yml` calls Preflight's reusable workflow with `composer ci`, and runs `refresh-patches` weekly (Mondays) and on demand.
- Green means the tests passed on all three PHP versions on both, and `composer ci` passed (on all three on GitHub, once on GitLab).

### Keeping the policy current[#](https://creed.apps.wayne.edu/docs/contributing.html#keeping-the-policy-current)

This is CREED's real maintenance job.

- **Patch levels are watched automatically.** `bin/refresh-patches.php` reads php.net (PHP), Packagist (Laravel), nodejs.org (Node) and endoflife.date (a PHP cross-check and Vue lines). It updates `latest_patch` and `latest_patch_checked`, and proposes new Vue lines. In CI the scheduled job is check-only: the refresh tool exits 3 when the policy changed and the job fails on the diff.
- **The policy robot opens the change every Monday.** `bin/policy-bot.php run` runs the fuller `bin/refresh-policy.php` (dates, patches, new lines), commits `policy/policy.json` and `policy/sources.json` on `auto/policy-refresh` and pushes a merge request labeled `auto-data`. It merges itself when the refresher exited 3 and the pipeline passes; after an exit 4 (something held or refused) it waits for a person, and each held or refused item has an `auto-alert` issue. It never tags or releases. Review steps and setup: [The policy robot](https://creed.apps.wayne.edu/docs/guides/policy-bot.html). The branch `auto/policy-refresh` must not be protected. The schedules live in the project's CI/CD settings on git.wayne.edu, not in this repo.
- **Support dates move only through review.** The robot writes a date that moves earlier or a later `active_until`, and holds a later `security_until` until two sources or 14 days agree. A person who edits a date by hand puts the upstream source in the commit message. End days are inclusive.
- **A red scheduled run is a to-do, not an outage:** run `php bin/refresh-patches.php`, read the diff, `composer ci`, add a CHANGELOG line, commit.
- **After any policy change,** the copies downstream are stale until refreshed. In each consumer (PROCTOR, Rollcall, Booster), run `php <creed>/bin/export.php --namespace='Waynestate\<Project>\Creed' --to=src/Creed`, then `composer creed-copy:check` with `CREED_PATH` pointing at this checkout. ADVISOR regenerates with `content:generate`.
- The schema is `version: 1`. Optional new fields keep it at 1; a breaking schema change needs a new version and a release of every reader. The older-reader contract is pinned by `tests/OlderReaderContractTest.php`; change the fixture only with a `schema_version` bump.

### Releasing[#](https://creed.apps.wayne.edu/docs/contributing.html#releasing)

1. Move the lines under `## Unreleased` in `CHANGELOG.md` to a new `## X.Y.Z (YYYY-MM-DD)` heading, leaving an empty `## Unreleased`. (0.1.0 predates the heading convention, so it has none.)
2. `composer ci` green locally, then on both pipelines for that commit.
3. Run a secrets scan of the history and check that nothing internal (server names, people, IDs) is in the tree.
4. Tag `X.Y.Z` (no `v`) on git.wayne.edu. The mirror carries the tag to GitHub, and Packagist picks it up from there.
5. A release needs a maintainer's approval. Never move or delete a published tag.
6. Then bump `waynestate/creed` where the stack pins it, and refresh the generated copies.

### The front page and its deploy[#](https://creed.apps.wayne.edu/docs/contributing.html#the-front-page-and-its-deploy)

`site/` is the static front page. It is served on Citadel at `https://creed.apps.wayne.edu/` (pre-production first) by the raw-PHP layer in `deploy/`: HELMET's headers in front, PROCTOR and this policy in the release. `deploy/` is its own Composer project, separate from the library. Most of it is generated by Squire (`deploy/.squire.json` records what), so regenerate it rather than hand-editing it. Only `deploy/public/index.php`, `deploy/public/.htaccess` and `deploy/composer.json` are written by hand. Run the parity kit with `deploy\scripts\parity.ps1` (Windows) or `deploy/scripts/parity.sh` (Linux and macOS).

When a stamp in `BEST_PRACTICES.md` changes, or a practice is added, update the front page in the same commit: the tally on the title page, the contents heading, that chapter's stamp bar and clause range, and the stamp on any clause the page reprints. `FrontPageTallyTest` recounts the stamps from `BEST_PRACTICES.md` and fails `composer ci` until `site/index.html` agrees; then run `composer site:agent-ready` so `site/index.md` and `llms-full.txt` follow.

### Things that trip people up[#](https://creed.apps.wayne.edu/docs/contributing.html#things-that-trip-people-up)

- `composer.json` pins Pinstripe for dev; PROCTOR warns on any `dev-main` pin.
- A scheduled `refresh-patches` failure is expected whenever upstream ships a patch.
- No em or en dashes anywhere in the docs; the handbook lint and the house style both care. Creed Bratton would not care, but he is not reviewing the merge request.

### Related[#](https://creed.apps.wayne.edu/docs/contributing.html#related)

- [Install](https://creed.apps.wayne.edu/docs/install.html)
- [Quick start](https://creed.apps.wayne.edu/docs/guides/quick-start.html)
- [Keeping the patches fresh](https://creed.apps.wayne.edu/docs/guides/patch-refresh.html)

## Carrying CREED in another package[#](https://creed.apps.wayne.edu/docs/guides/carrying-creed.html#carrying-creed-in-another-package)

This page explains who carries a copy of CREED's reader and policy, what the copy is, and how `bin/export.php` generates it and checks it.

### Who carries a copy[#](https://creed.apps.wayne.edu/docs/guides/carrying-creed.html#who-carries-a-copy)

- PROCTOR, Booster and Rollcall each carry a generated copy of the reader and policy under their own namespace, made by `bin/export.php`, so two tools in one app never fight over a class name.
- ADVISOR carries CREED's policy and handbook as a data bundle instead, in its `data/`.
- HELMET can read a `policy.json` at runtime, and apps and the stack's front-page deploys install `waynestate/creed` from Packagist.

### Why the copies began[#](https://creed.apps.wayne.edu/docs/guides/carrying-creed.html#why-the-copies-began)

The copies began because CREED was not on Packagist. It is now (`waynestate/creed`, 0.1.7 at this writing), so each copy can become a real `require`, one consumer at a time; until a consumer switches, its copy stays.

### Generating and checking the copy[#](https://creed.apps.wayne.edu/docs/guides/carrying-creed.html#generating-and-checking-the-copy)

CREED owns the generator and the check:

```
php bin/export.php --namespace=Waynestate\Proctor\Creed --to=vendor/creed-copy
php bin/export.php --check --namespace=Waynestate\Proctor\Creed --to=vendor/creed-copy
```

The copy is the reader with the namespace rewritten and `bundled()` repointed at its own `policy.json`; `--check` fails when the copy drifts from the source. Creed Bratton would have a form for this.

### Related[#](https://creed.apps.wayne.edu/docs/guides/carrying-creed.html#related)

- [The handbook](https://creed.apps.wayne.edu/docs/guides/handbook.html)
- [Reading the policy from PHP](https://creed.apps.wayne.edu/docs/guides/reading-the-policy.html)
- [Install](https://creed.apps.wayne.edu/docs/install.html)

## The handbook[#](https://creed.apps.wayne.edu/docs/guides/handbook.html#the-handbook)

This page maps the CREED handbook: what it is, how to read its key words and PROCTOR check lines, and where each of the thirteen chapters lives.

### What the handbook is[#](https://creed.apps.wayne.edu/docs/guides/handbook.html#what-the-handbook-is)

The rules for the Wayne State app stack, chapter by chapter. Each chapter states what the ADRs have decided or what WSU's developer standards (2024) already require, and names its undecided points under a "Not decided here" heading. The rules, chapter by chapter, live in the handbook site, built separately from `handbook/`.

### How to read a rule[#](https://creed.apps.wayne.edu/docs/guides/handbook.html#how-to-read-a-rule)

- The key words MUST, MUST NOT, SHOULD, SHOULD NOT and MAY in each chapter are to be interpreted as described in RFC 2119.
- A line that reads "PROCTOR check: `<id>`" names the PROCTOR check that reports a breach of that rule.

### The chapters[#](https://creed.apps.wayne.edu/docs/guides/handbook.html#the-chapters)

- [Versions](https://creed.apps.wayne.edu/handbook/versions.html): the stack's version policy, the state table from active to EOL plus 90 days, with the dates in `policy/policy.json` and every tool deriving a version's state from the date.
- [Dependencies](https://creed.apps.wayne.edu/handbook/dependencies.html): no unbounded constraints, a committed lock file, an audit with no advisories at or above the policy's severity threshold, and the private-packages registry rules.
- [Code](https://creed.apps.wayne.edu/handbook/code.html): PHP style with one Pint preset per repo, reading the code, static analysis at PHPStan level 8, banned patterns, and Vue and JavaScript linting.
- [Auth](https://creed.apps.wayne.edu/handbook/auth.html): one protocol-neutral library that returns a verified identity and leaves the session to the app, with its drivers and non-EOL PHP only.
- [Databases](https://creed.apps.wayne.edu/handbook/databases.html): the MySQL lines the policy lists, the conventions that keep an app working on the shared 5.6 server, and the 90-day grace period.
- [Runtime and headers](https://creed.apps.wayne.edu/handbook/runtime-and-headers.html): the runtime (Baseline) warns and refuses only for unsafe config, HELMET's headers on every response, proxy trust from a platform preset or the app's own list, and debug off in production.
- [Deploy gate](https://creed.apps.wayne.edu/handbook/deploy-gate.html): the gate runs PROCTOR against the commit being released, before it is released, and refuses EOL PHP.
- [CI](https://creed.apps.wayne.edu/handbook/ci.html): CI is enforcement point (c), a red pipeline before merge, built from Preflight's pinned components and judged with deterministic commands, never with a model.
- [Accessibility](https://creed.apps.wayne.edu/handbook/accessibility.html): WCAG 2.2 Level AA as the target for every public page, WayneUI components as the checked starting point, an automated Pa11y check in CI, and the open Title II question.
- [Every OS](https://creed.apps.wayne.edu/handbook/every-os.html): every developer tool works on Windows, macOS and Linux, with `.ps1` and `.sh` pairs, LF line endings and portable paths.
- [Secrets](https://creed.apps.wayne.edu/handbook/secrets.html): credentials never in version control and never in the served folder, with errors and debug output that hide them.
- [Production](https://creed.apps.wayne.edu/handbook/production.html): pre-production and production environments, running safely with the least access needed, and who can reach an app.
- [Overrides](https://creed.apps.wayne.edu/handbook/overrides.html): overrides are named, dated and visible, with an expiry date and a reason, and an expired override is a failure.

### Related[#](https://creed.apps.wayne.edu/docs/guides/handbook.html#related)

## The instance runner[#](https://creed.apps.wayne.edu/docs/guides/instance-runner.html#the-instance-runner)

This page explains why every product in the stack strongly recommends a git.wayne.edu instance runner, and where CREED's code lives.

### Strongly recommended: a git.wayne.edu instance runner[#](https://creed.apps.wayne.edu/docs/guides/instance-runner.html#strongly-recommended-a-git-wayne-edu-instance-runner)

git.wayne.edu now has an instance runner, and the stack's CI runs on it. Every product in the stack still strongly recommends a git.wayne.edu instance runner, so that capacity stays there.

![Creed Bratton from The Office in a dark suit and blue shirt with a wide, wild-eyed grin](https://creed.apps.wayne.edu/docs/readme/creed-bratton.gif)

Creed Bratton, whose quality assurance work we all admire. His past is a mystery. Ours is in `policy/policy.json`, where it belongs.

### Where the code lives[#](https://creed.apps.wayne.edu/docs/guides/instance-runner.html#where-the-code-lives)

The canonical repository is [enterprise-apps/creed](https://git.wayne.edu/enterprise-apps/creed) on git.wayne.edu. Open issues and merge requests there; tags are made there, by the maintainer, with an approver. CI runs on git.wayne.edu. GitHub ([waynestate/creed](https://github.com/waynestate/creed)) is a read-only push mirror of it: nobody pushes to it, and Packagist reads from it.

Creed Bratton would say the code lives wherever he last left it. Ours lives on git.wayne.edu.

## Keeping the patches fresh[#](https://creed.apps.wayne.edu/docs/guides/patch-refresh.html#keeping-the-patches-fresh)

This page explains how the patch-level data in `policy/policy.json` stays tied to the upstream feeds, and what the check-only scheduled job does when the refresh changes something.

### What the refresh does[#](https://creed.apps.wayne.edu/docs/guides/patch-refresh.html#what-the-refresh-does)

`bin/refresh-patches.php` re-reads the upstream feeds, rewrites the `latest_patch` fields in `policy/policy.json`, and proposes new Vue lines from endoflife.date. In doing so it updates `latest_patch` and `latest_patch_checked`.

### Where the data comes from[#](https://creed.apps.wayne.edu/docs/guides/patch-refresh.html#where-the-data-comes-from)

Patch levels are watched automatically. `bin/refresh-patches.php` reads php.net (PHP), Packagist (Laravel), nodejs.org (Node) and endoflife.date (a PHP cross-check and Vue lines).

### The check-only scheduled job[#](https://creed.apps.wayne.edu/docs/guides/patch-refresh.html#the-check-only-scheduled-job)

A scheduled CI job runs the refresh and is check-only: when the policy changed, the tool exits 3 and the job fails on the diff. A red scheduled run is a to-do, not an outage: run `php bin/refresh-patches.php`, read the diff, `composer ci`, add a CHANGELOG line, commit.

The committing path is the policy robot, covered in [The policy robot](https://creed.apps.wayne.edu/docs/guides/policy-bot.html): it runs the fuller `bin/refresh-policy.php` every Monday and opens a merge request, so a red check-only run usually has a robot merge request waiting beside it. The robot's schedule (`CREED_JOB=policy-bot`) does not run this job.

### Support dates[#](https://creed.apps.wayne.edu/docs/guides/patch-refresh.html#support-dates)

This script never touches a support date. Dates move in two reviewed ways only: the [policy robot](https://creed.apps.wayne.edu/docs/guides/policy-bot.html)'s Monday merge request, where `bin/refresh-policy.php` writes a date that moves earlier or a later `active_until`, and holds a later `security_until` until it is proven; or a person's own edit, with the upstream source in the commit message. End days are inclusive.

### Related[#](https://creed.apps.wayne.edu/docs/guides/patch-refresh.html#related)

- [Refreshing the policy](https://creed.apps.wayne.edu/docs/guides/policy-refresh.html)
- [The policy robot](https://creed.apps.wayne.edu/docs/guides/policy-bot.html)
- [Reading the policy from PHP](https://creed.apps.wayne.edu/docs/guides/reading-the-policy.html)
