Chapter 5

## Databases

9 sections · 25 provisions · **MUST** 4 · **SHOULD** 1 · **MAY** 1

Decided

Key words The key words **MUST**, **MUST NOT**, **SHOULD**, **SHOULD NOT** and **MAY** in this chapter are to be interpreted as described in [RFC 2119](https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc2119).

### [§5.1](https://creed.apps.wayne.edu/handbook/databases.html#what-the-stack-supports) What the stack supports

The policy lists the MySQL versions in [`policy/policy.json`](https://github.com/waynestate/creed/blob/main/policy/policy.json), under `mysql`: 5.6, 5.7, 8.0, 8.4 and 9.7, each with its [`active_until`](https://github.com/waynestate/creed/blob/main/policy/policy.json) and [`security_until`](https://github.com/waynestate/creed/blob/main/policy/policy.json) dates. The shared server runs 5.6, which is past security support; its `security_until` is 2021-02-28. Laravel 13 documents MySQL 5.7 or later. The conventions below keep an app working on the shared server until it is upgraded. They are a bridge, not the fix: the fix is the upgrade. Code that follows them runs unchanged on 8.4, so the move can be made With Arms Wide Open.

### [§5.2](https://creed.apps.wayne.edu/handbook/databases.html#which-mysql-lines-the-policy-lists) Which MySQL lines the policy lists

The policy lists the LTS lines, 8.4 and 9.7, for current use. It keeps the older lines, 5.6, 5.7 and 8.0, only to say that they are end of life. In MySQL 8.4 and later the default authentication plugin is `caching_sha2_password`: `mysql_native_password` is disabled by default in 8.4 and removed in 9.0. An app that **MUST** reach a server on the older plugin **MUST** set the server's plugin explicitly in its database config.

### [§5.3](https://creed.apps.wayne.edu/handbook/databases.html#grace-period) Grace period

An app **MAY** stay on a database version for 90 days after it leaves support, the policy's [`eol_grace_days`](https://github.com/waynestate/creed/blob/main/policy/policy.json); the version is `Eol` through that window and `EolGraceExpired` the day after, when the gate fails with no override. The window is a bridge for the upgrade, not a second support window: the fix is still the upgrade.

### [§5.4](https://creed.apps.wayne.edu/handbook/databases.html#names-comments-and-connections) Names, comments and connections

- Table and column names are descriptive. Add table and column comments (Laravel's `->comment()`) where the database supports them, to say what an element is for (**SHOULD**) (WSU developer standards, 2024).
- The connection between the app and the database **MUST** be encrypted. The database account **MUST** have only the privileges the app needs, never an administrator account (WSU developer standards, 2024).

### [§5.5](https://creed.apps.wayne.edu/handbook/databases.html#conventions-that-keep-5-6-working) Conventions that keep 5.6 working

- Set `Schema::defaultStringLength(191)` in `AppServiceProvider::boot()`, before any migration runs. 5.6 caps an indexed `utf8mb4` column at 767 bytes, which is 191 characters. [PROCTOR](https://proctor.apps.wayne.edu/) check: `mysql56`.
- Keep `utf8mb4` and `utf8mb4_unicode_ci`, the defaults. Never use an 8.0-only collation such as `utf8mb4_0900_ai_ci` (not yet confirmed on a 5.6 server).
- Store JSON as `text` or `longText`, with Eloquent `array` or `json` casts, and filter in PHP. 5.6 has no JSON column type. PROCTOR check: `mysql56`.
- Leave `use_upsert_alias` unset, so `upsert()` uses `VALUES()`. The row alias that setting switches to needs MySQL 8.0.19.
- Rename a column with raw `DB::statement('ALTER TABLE ... CHANGE ...')`. Avoid `renameColumn` and `renameIndex`, which emit 5.7 syntax. PROCTOR check: `mysql56`.
- Use `Schema::hasTable` only. Column introspection is not reliable on 5.6 (not yet confirmed on a 5.6 server).
- Skip `db:show` and `db:monitor`, and run one database-queue worker (or another driver if the platform offers one). 5.6 has no `SKIP LOCKED`, so a single worker avoids double-processing.
- Use `timestamp`, not `date`, for `useCurrent()`. A `date` column cannot take a current-timestamp default on 5.6.
- Run migrations in CI against a real 5.6 container. SQLite-only tests pass code that 5.6 rejects.

### [§5.6](https://creed.apps.wayne.edu/handbook/databases.html#avoid-until-the-server-is-upgraded) Avoid until the server is upgraded

#### [§5.6.1](https://creed.apps.wayne.edu/handbook/databases.html#schema) Schema

- JSON and jsonb columns
- Generated columns
- `renameIndex` and `renameColumn`
- Column introspection
- `invisible`, `instant` and `vector` columns
- InnoDB `spatialIndex` (needs 5.7.5, not yet confirmed on a 5.6 server)
- DESC indexes and CHECK constraints

#### [§5.6.2](https://creed.apps.wayne.edu/handbook/databases.html#queries) Queries

- `whereJson*` and JSON-path updates
- Window functions and CTEs
- `SKIP LOCKED` and `NOWAIT` in raw SQL
- `joinLateral`
- Joined deletes with an order or a limit

#### [§5.6.3](https://creed.apps.wayne.edu/handbook/databases.html#commands) Commands

- `db:show`
- `db:monitor`

### [§5.7](https://creed.apps.wayne.edu/handbook/databases.html#moving-to-8-4) Moving to 8.4

Code that follows the conventions and avoids the patterns above runs unchanged on 8.4. The server-side large-prefix settings (`innodb_large_prefix=ON`, `innodb_file_format=Barracuda`, DYNAMIC rows) are a question for the database owners, not something an app sets (not yet confirmed on a 5.6 server). Passing `ROW_FORMAT=DYNAMIC` through the `engine` config is likewise not yet confirmed on a 5.6 server.

Oracle moved 5.6 to Sustaining Support on 2021-02-01, so it gets no new fixes. Builds older than 5.6.46 also speak only TLS 1.0, which current hosts may refuse (not yet confirmed on a 5.6 server). Both are reasons to plan the move rather than wait for it.

### [§5.8](https://creed.apps.wayne.edu/handbook/databases.html#how-the-stack-checks-it) How the stack checks it

PROCTOR's `mysql56` check flags the patterns in the avoid list above that fail on 5.6: JSON columns, generated columns, `renameColumn`, long indexed strings and a missing `Schema::defaultStringLength(191)`. The rest of the list is not checked yet.

### [§5.9](https://creed.apps.wayne.edu/handbook/databases.html#sources) Sources

- Laravel 13 database docs: [https://laravel.com/docs/13.x/database](https://laravel.com/docs/13.x/database)
- Laravel docs, `migrations.md` (index-length section): [https://github.com/laravel/docs/blob/10.x/migrations.md](https://github.com/laravel/docs/blob/10.x/migrations.md)
- Laravel 13 migrations docs: [https://laravel.com/docs/13.x/migrations](https://laravel.com/docs/13.x/migrations)
- Laravel 13 query builder docs: [https://raw.githubusercontent.com/laravel/docs/13.x/queries.md](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/laravel/docs/13.x/queries.md)
- Laravel database queue: [https://github.com/laravel/framework/blob/13.x/src/Illuminate/Queue/DatabaseQueue.php](https://github.com/laravel/framework/blob/13.x/src/Illuminate/Queue/DatabaseQueue.php)
- Laravel schema builder: [https://github.com/laravel/framework/blob/13.x/src/Illuminate/Database/Schema/Builder.php](https://github.com/laravel/framework/blob/13.x/src/Illuminate/Database/Schema/Builder.php)
- MySQL 5.7.7 release notes: [https://dev.mysql.com/doc/relnotes/mysql/5.7/en/news-5-7-7.html](https://dev.mysql.com/doc/relnotes/mysql/5.7/en/news-5-7-7.html)
- MySQL 5.7.8 release notes (JSON): [https://dev.mysql.com/doc/relnotes/mysql/5.7/en/news-5-7-8.html](https://dev.mysql.com/doc/relnotes/mysql/5.7/en/news-5-7-8.html)
- MySQL 5.7.6 release notes (generated columns): [https://dev.mysql.com/doc/relnotes/mysql/5.7/en/news-5-7-6.html](https://dev.mysql.com/doc/relnotes/mysql/5.7/en/news-5-7-6.html)
- MySQL 5.6 CREATE INDEX (767 and 3072 byte limits): [https://dev.mysql.com/doc/refman/5.6/en/create-index.html](https://dev.mysql.com/doc/refman/5.6/en/create-index.html)
- MySQL 8.0, what is new: [https://dev.mysql.com/doc/refman/8.0/en/mysql-nutshell.html](https://dev.mysql.com/doc/refman/8.0/en/mysql-nutshell.html)
- MySQL CHECK constraints: [https://dev.mysql.com/doc/refman/8.0/en/create-table-check-constraints.html](https://dev.mysql.com/doc/refman/8.0/en/create-table-check-constraints.html)
- MySQL 5.7 INFORMATION_SCHEMA COLUMNS: [https://dev.mysql.com/doc/mysql-infoschema-excerpt/5.7/en/information-schema-columns-table.html](https://dev.mysql.com/doc/mysql-infoschema-excerpt/5.7/en/information-schema-columns-table.html)
- MySQL RENAME INDEX worklog: [https://dev.mysql.com/worklog/task/?id=6555](https://dev.mysql.com/worklog/task/?id=6555)
- MySQL INSERT ... ON DUPLICATE KEY UPDATE (row alias from 8.0.19): [https://dev.mysql.com/doc/refman/8.0/en/insert-on-duplicate.html](https://dev.mysql.com/doc/refman/8.0/en/insert-on-duplicate.html)
- Oracle MySQL end-of-life notices: [https://www.mysql.com/support/eol-notice.html](https://www.mysql.com/support/eol-notice.html)

In [`policy.json`](https://github.com/waynestate/creed/blob/main/policy/policy.json)

- **`components.*.versions.*.active_until`**: set per version
- **`rules.eol_grace_days`**: `90`
- **`components.*.versions.*.security_until`**: set per version

Chapter 2

## Dependencies

1 section · 15 provisions · **MUST NOT** 4 · **MUST** 6 · **SHOULD NOT** 1 · **SHOULD** 3

Decided

Key words The key words **MUST**, **MUST NOT**, **SHOULD**, **SHOULD NOT** and **MAY** in this chapter are to be interpreted as described in [RFC 2119](https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc2119).

- No `dev-master`, `dev-*` or `*` constraints on runtime dependencies (the stack's version policy). [PROCTOR](https://proctor.apps.wayne.edu/) check: `unbounded-constraints`.
- A lock file is required and **MUST** be committed (the stack's version policy). PROCTOR check: `lock-committed`.
- `composer audit` **MUST** report no advisories at or above the policy's severity threshold (the stack's version policy). PROCTOR check: `composer-audit`.

CREED's [`abandoned_packages`](https://github.com/waynestate/creed/blob/main/policy/policy.json) rule is `fail`, matching Composer's default since 2.7, so `composer audit` fails on an abandoned package. An app that has to keep one replaces it or records an override with a reason; PROCTOR's `composer-audit` check applies the same setting.

- `composer.json` `require.php` **MUST NOT** allow an EOL version as its lowest bound (the stack's version policy). PROCTOR check: `php-floor`.
- Apps **SHOULD** set a Composer cooldown of 3 days, once Composer 2.11 is stable and in the base images; until then no cooldown is set (the stack's dependency decision, 2026-11-03). A PROCTOR check for a missing cooldown is planned, not built.
- Every project is a framework-free core plus thin adapters. `composer.json` requires only `php` and PSR packages; Laravel, Inertia and Vue are `suggest` (the stack's core-plus-adapters design).
- Adapters call the core and never re-implement it (the stack's core-plus-adapters design).
- Before adding a third-party package, check it comes from a trusted source, and where the source is open, read enough of it to judge it sound and fit (**SHOULD**). The audit and abandoned-package rules in this chapter apply after that choice (WSU developer standards, 2024).

### [§2.1](https://creed.apps.wayne.edu/handbook/dependencies.html#private-packages) Private packages

- Internal-only packages **MUST** be installed from one GitLab package registry per ecosystem (Composer, npm), not from one `vcs`, `path` or `artifact` repository entry per package (the stack's private-packages decision).
- Credentials **MUST NOT** appear in any repository URL in `composer.json` or `composer.lock`, or as a literal value in a committed `.npmrc`. Tokens live in a gitignored `auth.json`, the npm user config, or a CI or build-time secret (the stack's private-packages decision). PROCTOR check: `repo-url-credentials`.
- Builds **MUST** use a read-only deploy token (`read_package_registry` only); personal access tokens **MUST NOT** be used in builds (the stack's private-packages decision).
- The private Composer registry entry **MUST** be canonical, and the Packagist entry **SHOULD** exclude the internal vendor names, so a public package with the same name can never be installed instead (the stack's private-packages decision).
- A released version **MUST** map to one commit for ever: tags are protected, and a version is never republished from a different commit (the stack's private-packages decision).
- Public code **MUST NOT** go through the private registry; it is published to Packagist or npm (the stack's private-packages decision).
- Apps **SHOULD NOT** proxy or mirror public registries in v1 (the stack's private-packages decision).

PROCTOR's `repo-url-credentials`, `package-sources` and `internal-vendor-shadowing` checks enforce rules 1, 2 and 4 (warning first), and [Preflight](https://preflight.apps.wayne.edu/)'s publish job enforces rule 5.

In [`policy.json`](https://github.com/waynestate/creed/blob/main/policy/policy.json)

- **`rules.abandoned_packages`**: `"fail"`

Set from [`handbook/dependencies.md` on GitHub](https://github.com/waynestate/creed/blob/main/handbook/dependencies.md), impression `218c65c`. Found a mistake? Fix the Markdown; this page is rebuilt from it.

Chapter 7

## Deploy gate

2 sections · 8 provisions

Decided

Key words The key words **MUST**, **MUST NOT**, **SHOULD**, **SHOULD NOT** and **MAY** in this chapter are to be interpreted as described in [RFC 2119](https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc2119).

The deploy gate runs [PROCTOR](https://proctor.apps.wayne.edu/) against the commit being released, before it is released, and refuses EOL PHP (the stack's deploy-gate decision).

- The deploy-time rule set is small, offline and fast: the target image's status and its PHP version against [`policy.json`](https://github.com/waynestate/creed/blob/main/policy/policy.json), the framework and stack package versions in `composer.lock`, and known advisories from a cached database (the stack's deploy-gate decision).
- EOL fails: a deploy that regresses a rule, a new app that fails any rule, or an expired override is blocked (the stack's deploy-gate decision).
- It ratchets: a deploy that doesn't make things worse always passes (the stack's deploy-gate decision).
- Each rule moves through stages, `report`, `warn`, `block`, with dates in `policy.json` (the stack's deploy-gate decision).

### [§7.1](https://creed.apps.wayne.edu/handbook/deploy-gate.html#on-citadel) On Citadel

- Citadel runs the gate in its release hook: `proctor gate` in `runGitPull()`, against the fetched commit, before it is checked out (the stack's deploy-gate decision).
- The gate is pending the Citadel team, which is still an open question. Until it is adopted, enforcement is CI on the test GitLab instance (the stack's deploy-gate decision).

### [§7.2](https://creed.apps.wayne.edu/handbook/deploy-gate.html#elsewhere) Elsewhere

- The same gate runs as a CI job through [Preflight](https://preflight.apps.wayne.edu/)'s `proctor` component, wherever the pipeline runs (first-repos).
- [Squire](https://squire.apps.wayne.edu/)'s `docker` target will run the gate before it ships an image, and so will its later `openshift` and `coolify` targets (the stack's rule that packages run on any container platform).

Set from [`handbook/deploy-gate.md` on GitHub](https://github.com/waynestate/creed/blob/main/handbook/deploy-gate.md), impression `a557384`. Found a mistake? Fix the Markdown; this page is rebuilt from it.

Source: https://creed.apps.wayne.edu/handbook/every-os.html

Chapter 10

## Every OS

5 provisions · **MUST** 1

Decided

Key words The key words **MUST**, **MUST NOT**, **SHOULD**, **SHOULD NOT** and **MAY** in this chapter are to be interpreted as described in [RFC 2119](https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc2119).

- Every developer tool works on Windows, macOS and Linux (the stack's every-OS design).
- A developer script ships as a `.ps1` and `.sh` pair that do the same thing, or as one PHP command, which works the same everywhere (the stack's every-OS design).
- Windows gets PowerShell (`.ps1`), which never needs bash or WSL. Linux and macOS get bash (`.sh`), written for macOS's stock bash 3.2 and its BSD tools (the stack's every-OS design).
- Every repo carries a `.gitattributes` with `* text=auto eol=lf`, and `.ps1`, `.bat` and `.cmd` set to CRLF. Anything that runs on a Linux host **MUST** be LF: on Citadel, and on OpenShift, Coolify or raw Docker elsewhere (the stack's every-OS design).
- Paths are built with the language's path functions, and subprocesses start with argument arrays, never shell strings (the stack's every-OS design). [PROCTOR](https://proctor.apps.wayne.edu/) check: `portability`.

Set from [`handbook/every-os.md` on GitHub](https://github.com/waynestate/creed/blob/main/handbook/every-os.md), impression `665c7ab`. Found a mistake? Fix the Markdown; this page is rebuilt from it.

Source: https://creed.apps.wayne.edu/handbook/

The handbook · 2026 Edition

## The CREED handbook

The rules for the Wayne State app stack, chapter by chapter. Each chapter states what the ADRs have decided or what WSU's developer standards (2024) already require, and names its undecided points under a "Not decided here" heading.

### How to read this book

- **[§3.2](https://creed.apps.wayne.edu/handbook/#contents)**: Chapter 3, section 2. Every section number is a link to itself: copy it to cite the rule.
- ****MUST** **SHOULD** **MAY****: The RFC 2119 key words, set in small capitals so a requirement never hides in a sentence.
- **(the stack's version policy)**: The decision a rule comes from. Rules state what is decided and cite it.
- **Not yet**: "To be decided": the gap is printed, and no rule is stated in its place.

[The whole book on one page](https://creed.apps.wayne.edu/handbook/print.html)

For printing, or for your browser's find. Every chapter, in order, from the same Markdown.

Chapter 13

## Overrides

5 provisions

Decided

Key words The key words **MUST**, **MUST NOT**, **SHOULD**, **SHOULD NOT** and **MAY** in this chapter are to be interpreted as described in [RFC 2119](https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc2119).

- Overrides are named, dated and visible (the stack's version policy).
- An app keeps a `policy-overrides.json` with an expiry date and a reason (the stack's version policy). [PROCTOR](https://proctor.apps.wayne.edu/) check: `overrides`.
- Check prints every override on every run, and Fleet lists them (the stack's version policy).
- An expired override is a failure (first-repos). PROCTOR check: `overrides`.
- On the Citadel side, overrides are held by Citadel admins, per app and per rule, with an expiry, a reason and an approver. There is no permanent override (the stack's deploy-gate decision).

Chapter 12

## Production

3 sections · 17 provisions · **MUST NOT** 3 · **MUST** 5 · **SHOULD** 3

Decided

Key words The key words **MUST**, **MUST NOT**, **SHOULD**, **SHOULD NOT** and **MAY** in this chapter are to be interpreted as described in [RFC 2119](https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc2119).

### [§12.1](https://creed.apps.wayne.edu/handbook/production.html#environments) Environments

- Every environment more than one person can reach follows the whole handbook; only a developer's own machine is exempt (WSU developer standards, 2024).
- Keep at least a pre-production and a production environment, each with its own working copy of every piece, database and supporting services included (WSU developer standards, 2024).
- Each deployment **SHOULD** be isolated from the others (one container per app), so one compromise does not become many. This holds on Citadel, OpenShift, Coolify and plain Docker (WSU developer standards, 2024). No check exists yet.
- Decide early whether the deployment is in disaster-recovery scope, and write the decision in the README (WSU developer standards, 2024).
- Back up anything kept outside source control, databases included. Say in the README how to restore one app (WSU developer standards, 2024).
- An app **SHOULD** be load tested in each environment where heavy use is expected (WSU developer standards, 2024). No check exists yet.

### [§12.2](https://creed.apps.wayne.edu/handbook/production.html#running-safely) Running safely

- The app and its scripts **MUST** run as a non-root, non-administrator user with the least access they need (WSU developer standards, 2024). No check exists yet.
- The web server **MUST NOT** list directory contents (WSU developer standards, 2024). No check exists yet.
- File permissions **MUST** be set per path; write access for the web server is granted only to specific files or folders, and mode `777` **MUST NOT** be used (WSU developer standards, 2024). [PROCTOR](https://proctor.apps.wayne.edu/) check: `world-writable` (`chmod 777` in scripts, Dockerfiles, CI and PHP).
- Debugging and diagnostic files, scripts, dumps and backups **MUST NOT** sit in the served folder (WSU developer standards, 2024). PROCTOR check: `served-folder` (`phpinfo()`, dumps, backups, logs, env files and `adminer*.php` under `public/`).
- On failure the app degrades predictably and fails closed: an authentication error withholds access (WSU developer standards, 2024).
- A person is told when something fails: a monitor calls `/up` on a schedule and alerts someone (WSU developer standards, 2024).
- Logs are rotated or removed at a set interval; temporary files are cleaned up; uploaded files have a retention rule. Citadel rotates container logs; elsewhere the platform or the app **MUST** (WSU developer standards, 2024). No check exists yet.
- Where it is practical, an app **SHOULD** record an audit trail of changes to data and of successful and failed access to sensitive data (WSU developer standards, 2024). No check exists yet.

Production is the encore. Keep the lights on and the doors locked, and the band plays on.

### [§12.3](https://creed.apps.wayne.edu/handbook/production.html#who-can-reach-it) Who can reach it

- Every app **MUST** set `robots.txt` to keep spiders out unless crawling is wanted (WSU developer standards, 2024). No check exists yet.
- Every app **MUST** limit access by network address to the audience it serves, as a second lock beside sign-in and never instead of it (WSU developer standards, 2024). No check exists yet.
- The one named exception: the stack's own public front pages are crawlable by design (the stack's agent-ready sites decision). It is a special case for those pages, not a general exemption for public pages.

Set from [`handbook/production.md` on GitHub](https://github.com/waynestate/creed/blob/main/handbook/production.md), impression `4e14fd3`. Found a mistake? Fix the Markdown; this page is rebuilt from it.

Chapter 6

## Runtime and headers

7 sections · 15 provisions · **MUST** 2 · **SHOULD NOT** 1

Decided

Key words The key words **MUST**, **MUST NOT**, **SHOULD**, **SHOULD NOT** and **MAY** in this chapter are to be interpreted as described in [RFC 2119](https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc2119).

### [§6.1](https://creed.apps.wayne.edu/handbook/runtime-and-headers.html#enforcement) Enforcement

- The runtime (Baseline) is enforcement point (a): it warns, and refuses only for unsafe config (the stack's enforcement design).

### [§6.2](https://creed.apps.wayne.edu/handbook/runtime-and-headers.html#headers) Headers

- Every response carries the same headers from [HELMET](https://helmet.apps.wayne.edu/) (the stack's runtime and headers design):
  - Content-Security-Policy: the [WayneUI](https://wayneui.apps.wayne.edu/) default policy plus a per-request nonce and `strict-dynamic`, with `frame-ancestors 'self'`, `base-uri 'self'`, `object-src 'none'` and `form-action 'self'` added.
  - X-Content-Type-Options `nosniff`.
  - X-Frame-Options `SAMEORIGIN`.
  - Referrer-Policy `strict-origin-when-cross-origin`.
  - Permissions-Policy, with camera, geolocation, microphone, payment and usb denied by default.
  - Cross-Origin-Opener-Policy `same-origin`.
  - Strict-Transport-Security `max-age=31536000; includeSubDomains`, on HTTPS responses only.
- Cross-Origin-Resource-Policy is off by default (the stack's runtime and headers design).
- An app **SHOULD NOT** weaken the default Content-Security-Policy with `'unsafe-inline'` for scripts; it uses the nonce instead (the stack's runtime and headers design). No check exists yet.

The headers are the setlist: the same one on every response. The HSTS encore plays only when the show is really on HTTPS.

### [§6.3](https://creed.apps.wayne.edu/handbook/runtime-and-headers.html#proxy-trust) Proxy trust

- Behind a proxy the app sees the proxy's address, so `X-Forwarded-Proto` is honored only from a trusted proxy (the stack's runtime and headers design).
- A platform preset (`citadel` or `docker`) names the trusted proxies; off the platform the app passes its own list. An unknown preset throws at boot (the stack's runtime and headers design).
- No Strict-Transport-Security is sent for a request that was not really secure (the stack's runtime and headers design).

### [§6.4](https://creed.apps.wayne.edu/handbook/runtime-and-headers.html#sessions) Sessions

- HELMET hardens the PHP session settings before the session starts (the stack's runtime and headers design).
- The request-forgery guard (Sec-Fetch-Site, then Origin) is optional and off by default; a rejected request gets 403 `Forbidden` (the stack's runtime and headers design).

### [§6.5](https://creed.apps.wayne.edu/handbook/runtime-and-headers.html#health) Health

- `/up` is the health endpoint HELMET answers for raw PHP apps (the stack's runtime and headers design).

### [§6.6](https://creed.apps.wayne.edu/handbook/runtime-and-headers.html#errors-in-production) Errors in production

- PHP `display_errors` **MUST** be `Off` and `log_errors` `On` in production ([Squire](https://squire.apps.wayne.edu/)'s deploy kit ships that php.ini; HELMET neither sets nor checks it). No check exists yet.
- Laravel `APP_DEBUG` **MUST** be `false` in production (WSU developer standards, 2024). The Laravel adapter writes one warning `helmet.debug_enabled_in_production` when it is true in the production environment.

A [PROCTOR](https://proctor.apps.wayne.edu/) check for this is proposed, not built.

### [§6.7](https://creed.apps.wayne.edu/handbook/runtime-and-headers.html#not-decided-here) Not decided here

- The Cross-Origin-Resource-Policy default.
- The Content-Security-Policy report endpoints.
- The metrics endpoint.

Set from [`handbook/runtime-and-headers.md` on GitHub](https://github.com/waynestate/creed/blob/main/handbook/runtime-and-headers.md), impression `48ebd53`. Found a mistake? Fix the Markdown; this page is rebuilt from it.

Source: https://creed.apps.wayne.edu/handbook/secrets.html

Chapter 11

## Secrets and debugging

3 sections · 9 provisions · **MUST NOT** 4 · **MUST** 3 · **SHOULD NOT** 1

Decided

Key words The key words **MUST**, **MUST NOT**, **SHOULD**, **SHOULD NOT** and **MAY** in this chapter are to be interpreted as described in [RFC 2119](https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc2119).

### [§11.1](https://creed.apps.wayne.edu/handbook/secrets.html#credentials) Credentials

- Credentials (database and service passwords, API keys, tokens) **MUST NOT** be committed to version control, because history keeps them forever. Commit `.env.example` with placeholders instead. A credential that was ever committed is treated as exposed and rotated (WSU developer standards, 2024). [PROCTOR](https://proctor.apps.wayne.edu/) checks: `app-key` (a committed `.env` or `APP_KEY`) and `repo-url-credentials` (a token in a package source URL); no general secret scan exists yet.
- Credentials and sensitive data **MUST** live outside any folder the web server serves. Laravel's `public/` is the only served folder; raw PHP apps serve one `public/` folder the same way (WSU developer standards, 2024). PROCTOR check: `served-folder` (dumps, backups, logs and env files in `public/`).
- The Laravel `APP_KEY` is a credential: whoever holds it can forge encrypted payloads, which can mean code execution. It **MUST NOT** be committed, a key that leaked **MUST** be rotated with `php artisan key:generate` on every environment that used it, and the session driver **SHOULD NOT** be `cookie`, which seals every session with the key (GitGuardian, exploiting public APP_KEY leaks). PROCTOR check: `app-key`.
- An app uses its own dedicated application ID, never a person's employee or student AccessID, to reach another server or service, with the fewest permissions the task needs (WSU developer standards, 2024).
- Real values come from the environment at deploy time (the Citadel dashboard or CI variables), never from a file in the repo (WSU developer standards, 2024).

### [§11.2](https://creed.apps.wayne.edu/handbook/secrets.html#errors-and-debug-output) Errors and debug output

- `APP_DEBUG` **MUST** be `false` in production (WSU developer standards, 2024). The Laravel adapter writes one warning `helmet.debug_enabled_in_production` when it is true in the production environment. A PROCTOR check for this is proposed, not built.
- Public-facing code **MUST NOT** display default interpreter or framework error pages to the user; show a controlled message and log the detail (WSU developer standards, 2024). No check exists yet.
- Logs and diagnostic output **MUST NOT** contain credentials or personally identifiable information such as Social Security numbers. That includes logged exceptions (WSU developer standards, 2024). No check exists yet.

A leaked password is a bad encore: everyone remembers it, and nobody asked for a second showing.

### [§11.3](https://creed.apps.wayne.edu/handbook/secrets.html#not-decided-here) Not decided here

- The [HELMET](https://helmet.apps.wayne.edu/) header rules and runtime refusals are written in `runtime-and-headers.md`.

Set from [`handbook/secrets.md` on GitHub](https://github.com/waynestate/creed/blob/main/handbook/secrets.md), impression `0c8f1e9`. Found a mistake? Fix the Markdown; this page is rebuilt from it.

Source: https://creed.apps.wayne.edu/handbook/versions.html

Chapter 1

## Versions

4 sections · 4 provisions · **MUST NOT** 2 · **MUST** 3

Decided

Key words The key words **MUST**, **MUST NOT**, **SHOULD**, **SHOULD NOT** and **MAY** in this chapter are to be interpreted as described in [RFC 2119](https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc2119).

The stack's version policy states:

Table 1-1

| State | Runtime (Baseline) | Check / CI | Platform |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| active | silent | pass |  |
| security-only | ribbon warning in non-production; log line in production | warning |  |
| EOL | ribbon error in non-production; daily log line | fail | Citadel retires the image on its own schedule; elsewhere the owner retires it, and the gate fails either way |
| EOL + 90 days | as above | fail; no override |  |

- The dates live in [`policy/policy.json`](https://github.com/waynestate/creed/blob/main/policy/policy.json). Every tool derives a version's state from the date, through the CREED reader. No other code decides state (the stack's version policy).
- The PHP floor is `^8.2`, the oldest non-EOL version today (the stack's version policy). It moves to `^8.3` on 2027-01-01. [PROCTOR](https://proctor.apps.wayne.edu/) check: `php-floor`.
- Stack packages raise their own `php` floor in a new major when a PHP version reaches EOL, so security fixes require the upgrade (the stack's version policy).
- `policy.json` is a contract, versioned like [WayneUI](https://wayneui.apps.wayne.edu/)'s `/v2/`. Older Check versions **MUST** still read newer policy files (the stack's version policy).

### [§1.1](https://creed.apps.wayne.edu/handbook/versions.html#latest-patches) Latest patches

Each version can also carry a [`latest_patch`](https://github.com/waynestate/creed/blob/main/policy/policy.json): the newest patch release for that version as of a [`latest_patch_checked`](https://github.com/waynestate/creed/blob/main/policy/policy.json) date. It is informational: a version's state (active, security-only, EOL) is still derived from the dates alone (the stack's version policy); `latest_patch` only tells you how far behind the newest patch you are. `bin/refresh-patches.php` keeps it current by reading the four upstream feeds (php.net's active releases, Packagist's `laravel/framework`, nodejs.org's dist index, and endoflife.date's PHP data) and writing `latest_patch` and `latest_patch_checked` for every version the feeds cover; a version the feeds do not cover (an EOL branch, for instance) is left as-is with a warning, and a php.net / endoflife.date disagreement is reported but never fails the run. Run it with `--dry-run` to preview, or `--offline <dir>` to test against saved feeds.

### [§1.2](https://creed.apps.wayne.edu/handbook/versions.html#base-images) Base images

A base image **MUST** be rebuilt when the policy's `latest_patch` for its branch changes; the policy robot opens that change, so an image never sits behind the patch level the policy records (the stack's version policy). Every such change to `latest_patch` is a rebuild. An image **MUST NOT** be pinned to a branch the policy marks EOL (the stack's version policy).

`images.docker` names the official image for a plain Docker target. Citadel names its own images, so `images.citadel` stays unset until Citadel publishes names. `openshift` and `coolify` are not filled yet.

### [§1.3](https://creed.apps.wayne.edu/handbook/versions.html#node) Node

The policy lists even Node majors only, because even majors are the LTS lines; odd majors **MUST NOT** be a target and are not listed (the stack's version policy).

An app **MUST** build on a Node line that has not reached end of life. PROCTOR check: `node-eol`. It reads `.nvmrc`, `.node-version`, `volta.node` and the `node` image in CI and Dockerfiles: an active line passes, a security-only line warns and an EOL line fails. `engines.node` and an odd major warn.

### [§1.4](https://creed.apps.wayne.edu/handbook/versions.html#tool-minimums) Tool minimums

The `tools` block sets a minimum version for a developer tool. Each key is a tool name, each value a `minimum` version. Today it holds Composer at 2.8.0.

Composer 2.8.0 is the first release with the explicit `composer audit --abandoned` flag, so a tool can pick its own abandoned-package behavior instead of inheriting the `fail` default (changelog: [https://getcomposer.org/changelog/2.8.0](https://getcomposer.org/changelog/2.8.0)).

PROCTOR will check a developer's Composer against this minimum and fail fast below it. PROCTOR check: `composer-version`. The minimum is a floor, not a ceiling: we do not go lower, no matter how the crowd sings for more.

In [`policy.json`](https://github.com/waynestate/creed/blob/main/policy/policy.json)

- **`components.*.versions.*.latest_patch`**: set per version
- **`components.*.versions.*.latest_patch_checked`**: set per version

Set from [`handbook/versions.md` on GitHub](https://github.com/waynestate/creed/blob/main/handbook/versions.md), impression `aa147fa`. Found a mistake? Fix the Markdown; this page is rebuilt from it.
